title.en: Volume 332 Biographies 119: Fu Leihun, Wen Shou, Liu Bingtian, Cha Li, E Bao, Yan Xishen, Xu Ji, Jue Luo Tu Si De, Zhang Bao, Xu Siceng, Chen Buying, Sun Yongqing, Guo Shixun, Bi Yuan
title.raw: 卷332 列傳一百十九 富勒浑 文绶 刘秉恬 查礼 鄂宝 颜希深 徐绩 觉罗图思德 彰宝 徐嗣曾 陈步瀛 孙永清 郭世勋 毕沅

sentences.zh: 列傳一百十九

translations.literal: Biography 119
translations.idiomatic: Biography 119

sentences.zh: 富勒渾文綬劉秉恬查禮鄂寶顏希深徐績

translations.literal: Fu Leihun, Wen Shou, Liu Bingtian, Cha Li, E Bao, Yan Xishen, Xu Ji
translations.idiomatic: Fu Leihun, Wen Shou, Liu Bingtian, Cha Li, E Bao, Yan Xishen, Xu Ji

sentences.zh: 覺羅圖思德彰寶徐嗣曾陳步瀛孫永清

translations.literal: Jueluo Tusi De, Zhang Bao, Xu Siceng, Chen Buying, Sun Yongqing
translations.idiomatic: Jueluo Tusi De, Zhang Bao, Xu Siceng, Chen Buying, Sun Yongqing

sentences.zh: 郭世勳畢沅

translations.literal: Guo Shixun, Bi Yuan
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shixun, Bi Yuan

sentences.zh: 富勒渾，章佳氏。

translations.literal: Fu Leihun, of the Zhangjia clan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Leihun was of the Zhangjia clan.

sentences.zh: 初自舉人授內閣中書。

translations.literal: At first, from the rank of provincial graduate he was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service as a Grand Secretariat secretary on the strength of his provincial graduate degree.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶部郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to be a director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十八年，授山西冀寧道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of the Qianlong reign, he was appointed intendant of the Jin-Ning Circuit in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1763, the twenty-eighth year of Qianlong, he was appointed intendant of the Jin-Ning Circuit in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 遷山東按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be judicial commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to judicial commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 以在冀寧道失察陽曲知縣段成功虧帑，左授山西雁平道。

translations.literal: Because while intendant of the Jin-Ning Circuit he had failed to detect that Yangqu magistrate Duan Chenggong had embezzled public funds, he was demoted and appointed intendant of the Yan-Ping Circuit in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as Jin-Ning intendant he had failed to detect embezzlement by Yangqu magistrate Duan Chenggong and was demoted to intendant of the Yan-Ping Circuit in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 再遷浙江布政使。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to be provincial treasurer of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to provincial treasurer of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, he served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year he acted as governor.

sentences.zh: 奏劾總督崔應階僕誣指錢塘民為賊，擅刑致斃，論罪如律。

translations.literal: He memorialized impeaching Governor-General Cui Yingjie's servant for falsely accusing a Qiantang commoner of being a bandit, illegally torturing him and causing his death; punishment was determined according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Governor-General Cui Yingjie's servant for falsely denouncing a Qiantang townsman as a bandit, torturing him without authority until he died, and secured conviction under the statute.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，調陝西。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, he was transferred to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he was transferred to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 尋擢湖廣總督，入覲，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang; he attended court and was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted governor-general of Huguang, presented himself at court, and received a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 四川總督阿爾泰坐貪黷玩縱得罪，上命富勒渾如四川，會總督文綬按治。

translations.literal: Sichuan Governor-General A'ertai was punished for corruption, dereliction, and indulgence; the Emperor ordered Fu Leihun to proceed to Sichuan and join Governor-General Wen Shou in conducting the investigation.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichuan Governor-General A'ertai was condemned for graft, lax discipline, and indulgence, the Emperor sent Fu Leihun to Sichuan to investigate jointly with Governor-General Wen Shou.

sentences.zh: 阿爾泰縱子明德布與布政使劉益相結受賕，明德佈在京師，上令軍機大臣傳訊，自承，富勒渾奏論益立斬。

translations.literal: A'ertai indulged his son Mingdebu, who colluded with provincial treasurer Liu Yi to accept bribes; Mingdebu was in the capital, and the Emperor ordered the Grand Council to interrogate him; he confessed, and Fu Leihun memorialized that Yi should be executed immediately.
translations.idiomatic: A'ertai had allowed his son Mingdebu to collude with Provincial Treasurer Liu Yi in taking bribes; Mingdebu was in Beijing, and when the Grand Council interrogated him on imperial order he confessed; Fu Leihun then urged that Yi be summarily executed.

sentences.zh: 上以為過重，改監候，獄連署布政使李本，富勒渾奏本罪當奪職，枷示不足蔽辜，請留軍效力。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered this too severe and changed it to imprisonment awaiting execution; the case implicated Acting Provincial Treasurer Li Ben; Fu Leihun memorialized that Ben's offense warranted dismissal from office, that cangue display was insufficient to cover his guilt, and requested that he be retained to serve with the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor deemed this excessive and commuted it to imprisonment awaiting execution; Acting Provincial Treasurer Li Ben was implicated, and Fu Leihun argued that dismissal alone and cangue display would not answer the crime, asking that Ben be kept with the army on active service.

sentences.zh: 上責其名重實寬，意存取巧，命枷示期滿，留軍效力。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked him for a severe name but lenient reality, intending to take an easy way out, and ordered cangue display for the full term, then retention to serve with the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked him for severity in word but leniency in deed and for trying to find a loophole, and ordered Ben displayed in the cangue for the full term before serving with the army.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，師徵金川，四川總督劉秉恬出駐美諾，命富勒渾留署四川總督，總理各路軍需。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, when the army campaigned against Jinchuan, Sichuan Governor-General Liu Bingtian went out to garrison Meinuo; Fu Leihun was ordered to remain as acting Sichuan governor-general and to oversee military supplies on all routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year, during the Jinchuan campaign, Liu Bingtian went forward to Meinuo while Fu Leihun was left acting governor-general of Sichuan in charge of supplies on every route.

sentences.zh: 秉恬奏：「揀發往川省各員視軍營為畏途，惟恐出口辦差不通聞問。」

translations.literal: Bingtian memorialized: "Officials selected and sent to Sichuan regard the army camps as a road to dread and fear only to go beyond the passes on assignment and lose touch with news."
translations.idiomatic: Bingtian reported that newly dispatched officials treated service beyond the passes as a dreaded posting and dreaded losing contact once they left.

sentences.zh: 上以責富勒渾，富勒渾奏陳：「司道公議，新到各員出口辦差，未免竭蹶。

translations.literal: The Emperor blamed Fu Leihun; Fu Leihun memorialized: "The circuit intendants jointly agreed that newly arrived officials going beyond the passes on assignment would inevitably be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor held Fu Leihun responsible; Fu Leihun replied that the circuit intendants had jointly agreed that new arrivals sent beyond the passes would be overstrained.

sentences.zh: 請以現任各員調赴，而令新到者分別署理。」

translations.literal: He requested that incumbent officials be transferred thither, while newly arrived ones be assigned to act in their posts respectively."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that current officials be sent forward while newcomers act in their stead.

sentences.zh: 上責富勒渾玩公沽譽，令劾倡議者，富勒渾奏司道公議，並無倡始。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked Fu Leihun for treating public duty lightly and currying reputation, and ordered him to impeach those who had initiated the proposal; Fu Leihun memorialized that it was a joint opinion of the circuit intendants and that no one had initiated it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accused Fu Leihun of shirking duty to win praise and ordered him to impeach the ringleaders; Fu Leihun reported that the intendants had deliberated together and that no one had originated the plan.

sentences.zh: 上益不懌，謂：「富勒渾竟敢以罰不及眾哧朕！」

translations.literal: The Emperor grew still more displeased and said: "Fu Leihun actually dares to frighten Us by saying punishment cannot reach the multitude!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grew angrier still, declaring that Fu Leihun dared intimidate him with the claim that the many could not all be punished.

sentences.zh: 下部議，奪官，命寬之。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Board for deliberation; his office was to be stripped, but the Emperor ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the boards for sentence; dismissal was proposed, but the Emperor ordered clemency.

sentences.zh: 木果木師潰，底木達被陷。

translations.literal: The army was routed at Mugongmu, and Dimuda fell.
translations.idiomatic: The army was shattered at Mugongmu and Dimuda was lost.

sentences.zh: 富勒渾率新至貴州兵馳赴蒙固橋防守，事聞，上嘉之。

translations.literal: Fu Leihun led newly arrived Guizhou troops in haste to defend the Menggu Bridge; when this was reported, the Emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Leihun rushed newly arrived Guizhou troops to hold the Menggu Bridge; the Emperor commended him when he heard.

sentences.zh: 旋奪秉恬官，即以富勒渾實授，令駐美諾，以欽差大臣關防督餉。

translations.literal: Soon Bingtian was stripped of office, and Fu Leihun was appointed in full, ordered to garrison Meinuo and to supervise provisions with the seal of an imperial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Bingtian was soon dismissed and Fu Leihun appointed in his place, stationed at Meinuo with an imperial commissioner's seal to supervise grain.

sentences.zh: 時美諾亦被陷，富勒渾屯明郭宗河口，據山梁設卡防守，復發兵分駐路頂宗、巴朗拉。

translations.literal: At that time Meinuo too had fallen; Fu Leihun encamped at the Mingguozong River mouth, held the mountain ridge with checkpoints for defense, and again sent troops to garrison separately at Ludingzong and Balangla.
translations.idiomatic: Meinuo had also fallen; Fu Leihun held the Mingguozong river mouth, fortified the ridge with checkpoints, and detached troops to Ludingzong and Balangla.

sentences.zh: 將軍阿桂進攻小金川，上命富勒渾與提督王進泰統兵策應。

translations.literal: General Agui advanced against Lesser Jinchuan; the Emperor ordered Fu Leihun and Regional Commander Wang Jintai to command troops in support.
translations.idiomatic: As General Agui attacked Lesser Jinchuan, the Emperor ordered Fu Leihun and Regional Commander Wang Jintai to coordinate supporting forces.

sentences.zh: 師克美諾，上令富勒渾、進泰嚴守美諾，並分兵駐僧格宗、明郭宗。

translations.literal: When the army took Meinuo, the Emperor ordered Fu Leihun and Jintai to hold Meinuo strictly and to detach troops to garrison Senggezong and Mingguozong.
translations.idiomatic: After Meinuo was recovered, the Emperor ordered Fu Leihun and Jintai to hold it firmly and post detachments at Senggezong and Mingguozong.

sentences.zh: 阿桂奏富勒渾、王進泰通慎而葸，於山川形勢、行軍機要均未能悉，請令副都統成果、雲南提督常青駐守後路，上從之，諭戒富勒渾等勿存畛域。

translations.literal: Agui memorialized that Fu Leihun and Wang Jintai were overly cautious and timid, that they did not fully understand terrain or the essentials of campaigning, and requested that Vice Commander-in-Chief Chengguo and Yunnan Regional Commander Changqing guard the rear; the Emperor assented and admonished Fu Leihun and the others not to keep to their own jurisdictions.
translations.idiomatic: Agui reported that Fu Leihun and Wang Jintai were excessively cautious and ignorant of terrain and campaign essentials, and asked that Vice Commander Chengguo and Yunnan Regional Commander Changqing hold the rear; the Emperor agreed and warned Fu Leihun not to stand on territorial pride.

sentences.zh: 奏新開楸底至色利溝運道，軍糧歸此路運送。

translations.literal: He memorialized opening a transport route from Qiudi to Seligou, with army grain to be moved by this road.
translations.idiomatic: He reported a new haul road from Qiudi to Seligou and proposed routing army grain along it.

sentences.zh: 瑪爾當、明郭宗諸地存米，借防兵一月糧，餘俱運軍前，請撤前設台站；

translations.literal: Stored grain at Ma'erdang, Mingguozong, and other places was lent to garrison troops for one month's rations; the remainder was all sent to the front, and he requested withdrawal of previously established courier stations;
translations.idiomatic: Grain stored at Ma'erdang and Mingguozong was issued to garrisons for one month's rations, the surplus sent forward, and earlier courier stations asked to be dismantled;

sentences.zh: 又奏分兵駐防大板昭及梭格泊古諸地。

translations.literal: He also memorialized detaching troops to garrison Daban Zhao and Suogebogu and other places.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed garrison detachments at Daban Zhao, Suogebogu, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 四十年，奏阿桂等督兵進搗賊巢，應用糧餉、軍火、銅片、砲料，儲備充裕，並造皮船濟師；

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he memorialized that Agui and others, leading troops to strike the rebel nest, had ample stores of grain, pay, munitions, copper sheets, and artillery materials, and had also built leather boats to ferry the army;
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he reported that Agui's advance on the rebel stronghold was supplied with grain, pay, munitions, copper, and gunpowder, and that leather boats had been built to ferry troops;

sentences.zh: 又奏調梭格泊古、瑪爾當兵分防沙壩、三松坪，以護運道：皆稱旨。

translations.literal: He also memorialized transferring troops from Suogebogu and Ma'erdang to guard Shaba and Sansongping to protect the transport route: all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also moved troops from Suogebogu and Ma'erdang to guard Shaba and Sansongping for the supply line—all approved.

sentences.zh: 上命富勒渾駐布朗郭宗，富勒渾奏阿桂、明亮合攻甲索山梁，布朗郭宗距軍五百餘裡，慮難於策應。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Fu Leihun to garrison Bulangguozong; Fu Leihun memorialized that Agui and Mingliang were jointly attacking the Jiasuo ridge, that Bulangguozong was more than five hundred li from the army, and that he feared difficulty in coordinating support.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to Bulangguozong, Fu Leihun noted that Agui and Mingliang were attacking the Jiasuo ridge five hundred li away and that he could hardly coordinate from so far.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「阿桂進攻勒烏圍，自應隨軍督餉。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed: "When Agui advances against Lewuwei, he should naturally follow the army to supervise provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied that when Agui advanced on Lewuwei, Fu Leihun should follow the army to supervise supplies.

sentences.zh: 兵事移步換形，不必泥前旨也。」

translations.literal: Military affairs shift step by step; there is no need to cling to an earlier instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns change shape from day to day; he need not be bound by the earlier order."

sentences.zh: 師克勒烏圍，奏請撤前設卓克採一路台站。

translations.literal: When the army took Lewuwei, he memorialized requesting withdrawal of courier stations along the Zhuokecai route.
translations.idiomatic: After Lewuwei fell he asked to close the Zhuokecai courier stations.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，复授湖廣總督，命師還上官。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he was again appointed governor-general of Huguang and ordered to return to his post when the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year he was reappointed governor-general of Huguang and told to resume his post when the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 金川平，議敘。

translations.literal: When Jinchuan was pacified, rewards were deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jinchuan pacification, merits were recorded for reward.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，授禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year he became Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，調工部。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was transferred to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year he was moved to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 授鑲藍旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: He was appointed commander-in-chief of the Mongol Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander of the Mongol Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，复授湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was again appointed governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year he returned as governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，調閩浙，上南巡，迎謁。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was transferred to Fujian-Zhejiang; when the Emperor made a southern tour, he went out to welcome and attend.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he was transferred to Fujian-Zhejiang and met the Emperor on the southern tour.

sentences.zh: 時李侍堯以貪縱得罪，富勒渾入對，上諭及之。

translations.literal: At that time Li Shiyao was punished for greed and indulgence; Fu Leihun entered audience, and the Emperor spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiyao had just been condemned for corruption; in audience the Emperor raised the case with Fu Leihun.

sentences.zh: 富勒渾對：「侍堯實心體國，為督撫中所罕見。」

translations.literal: Fu Leihun replied: "Shiyao is sincere in serving the state and is rarely seen among governors and governors-general."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Leihun answered that Shiyao served the dynasty wholeheartedly, a rarity among provincial chiefs.

sentences.zh: 及上命各督撫議罪，又請行誅，上責其前後歧異。

translations.literal: When the Emperor ordered all governors and governors-general to deliberate punishment, he again asked for execution; the Emperor rebuked his inconsistency.
translations.idiomatic: When governors were asked to recommend sentences, he then urged execution; the Emperor rebuked his reversal.

sentences.zh: 浙江巡撫王亶望丁憂，留辦塘工，攜家居杭州。

translations.literal: Zhejiang Governor Wang Tanwang was in mourning but remained to manage the seawall works and kept his household in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wang Tanwang, though in mourning, stayed to oversee seawall works and kept his family in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 亶望得罪，上又責富勒渾未劾。

translations.literal: When Tanwang was condemned, the Emperor again blamed Fu Leihun for not having impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tanwang fell, the Emperor faulted Fu Leihun for failing to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 大學士阿桂赴浙江閱海塘，疏劾杭嘉湖道王燧，又責富勒渾徇庇。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Agui went to Zhejiang to inspect the seawall, memorialized impeaching Hang-Jia-Hu Circuit Intendant Wang Sui, and again blamed Fu Leihun for favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Agui, inspecting the seawall, impeached Circuit Intendant Wang Sui and accused Fu Leihun of shielding him.

sentences.zh: 奪孔雀翎，降三品頂帶，授河南巡撫。

translations.literal: His peacock feather was taken, his rank insignia reduced to third grade, and he was appointed governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his peacock feather and third-grade insignia and was made governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 河溢萬錦灘，富勃渾親赴防護；

translations.literal: When the river overflowed at Wanjin Beach, Fu Leihun went in person to oversee defenses;
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River broke at Wanjin Beach, Fu Leihun went personally to the works;

sentences.zh: 又溢青龍岡，四十七年，工竟，還現任頂帶。

translations.literal: It overflowed again at Qinglong Hill; in the forty-seventh year the works were completed and his former rank insignia was restored.
translations.idiomatic: A second breach at Qinglong Hill followed; in the forty-seventh year the repairs finished and his insignia was restored.

sentences.zh: 复授閩浙總督。

translations.literal: He was again appointed governor-general of Fujian-Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed again governor-general of Fujian-Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 台灣漳、泉民械鬥，劾總兵金蟾桂、知府蘇泰等，並奪官。

translations.literal: When Zhangzhou and Quanzhou people in Taiwan fought with weapons, he impeached Regional Commander Jin Changui, Prefect Su Tai, and others, and they were all stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: After armed clashes between Zhangzhou and Quanzhou settlers in Taiwan, he impeached Regional Commander Jin Changui and Prefect Su Tai, who were all dismissed.

sentences.zh: 五十年三月，入京，與千叟宴。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fiftieth year he entered the capital and attended the banquet for a thousand elders.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fiftieth year he came to the capital for the banquet of a thousand elders.

sentences.zh: 調兩廣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 粵海關監督穆騰額入覲，上詢富勒渾操守，對：「未敢深信。」

translations.literal: Superintendent of the Guangdong Customs Muteng'e came to audience; the Emperor asked about Fu Leihun's integrity, and he replied: "I do not yet dare fully trust it."
translations.idiomatic: Customs Superintendent Muteng'e, at audience, said he could not yet fully trust Fu Leihun's integrity when asked.

sentences.zh: 及命軍機大臣詰之，又發富勒渾縱僕殷士俊納賕狀，下巡撫孫士毅按治。

translations.literal: When the Grand Council was ordered to press him further, he also exposed Fu Leihun's allowing his servant Yin Shijun to take bribes; the case was sent to Governor Sun Shiyi for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by the Grand Council, he exposed Fu Leihun's servant Yin Shijun taking bribes; Governor Sun Shiyi was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 士俊常熟人，並令江蘇織造四德等籍其家資累萬；

translations.literal: Shiyi was a native of Changshu; the Jiangsu weaving superintendent Side and others were also ordered to register his household assets, which amounted to tens of thousands;
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi was from Changshu; weaving officials were told to inventory his property, worth tens of thousands;

sentences.zh: 士毅奏亦發富勒渾與士俊等關通納賄事實，上奪富勒渾官，遣尚書舒常如廣東會訊。

translations.literal: Shiyi's memorial also exposed Fu Leihun's collusion with Shiyi and others in taking bribes; the Emperor stripped Fu Leihun of office and sent Minister Shu Chang to Guangdong to conduct a joint inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi's report implicated Fu Leihun in bribery with him and others; Fu Leihun was dismissed and Minister Shu Chang sent to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 大學士阿桂方按事浙江，又命士毅逮富勒渾監送阿桂鞫治，論斬，下刑部獄。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Agui was then investigating affairs in Zhejiang; Shiyi was also ordered to arrest Fu Leihun and escort him under guard to Agui for trial; the sentence was death, and he was imprisoned in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Agui was investigating in Zhejiang; Shiyi was to arrest Fu Leihun and deliver him for trial; death was recommended and he was held in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，詔釋之。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year an edict released him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year an edict pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，坐在閩浙失察總兵柴大紀貪劣，復下刑部論紋，仍釋之。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year, for failure while in Fujian-Zhejiang to detect the corruption of Regional Commander Chai Daji, he was again sent to the Ministry of Punishments for the death penalty by strangulation, but was again released.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year he was again sentenced to strangulation for not detecting Regional Commander Chai Daji's corruption in Fujian-Zhejiang, then pardoned again.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，羅源盜發，上追論富勒渾廢弛玩誤，戍伊犁。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year, when bandits rose in Luoyuan, the Emperor revisited Fu Leihun's laxity and negligence and exiled him to Yili.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year, after banditry in Luoyuan, the Emperor banished him to Yili for past negligence.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，釋回。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year he was released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year he was released and returned home.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，又發熱河，是年即釋回。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year he was again sent to Rehe; that same year he was released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year he was sent to Rehe, then released the same year.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 文綬，富察氏，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Wen Shou, of the Fuca clan, a Bannerman of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Shou, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，自監生授內閣中書。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of the Yongzheng reign, from the rank of student of the Imperial Academy he was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng (1735) he became a Grand Secretariat secretary from the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 再遷禮部員外郎，改內閣侍讀。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Rites and transferred to be a reader in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director in the Ministry of Rites, then became a Grand Secretariat reader.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十一年，授甘肅涼州知府。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of the Qianlong reign, he was appointed prefect of Liangzhou in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Qianlong he was appointed prefect of Liangzhou in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 累遷轉山西布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly and transferred to be provincial treasurer of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly until he became provincial treasurer of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，坐迎合巡撫和其衷徇陽曲知縣段成功虧帑，奪官，戍軍台。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, for currying favor with Governor He Qi'zhong and indulging Yangqu magistrate Duan Chenggong in embezzling public funds, he was stripped of office and sent to serve at a military post.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was dismissed and sent to the military posts for colluding with Governor He Qi'zhong to shield Duan Chenggong's embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 旋授道銜，往哈密辦事。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the rank of circuit intendant and sent to handle affairs at Hami.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given intendant rank and sent to Hami on assignment.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，授河南巡撫，未上官，調陝西。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was appointed governor of Henan; before assuming office he was transferred to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he was named governor of Henan but transferred to Shaanxi before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，署陝甘總督。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he served as acting governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year he acted as governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu.

sentences.zh: 土爾扈特內附，命赴齊齊哈爾犒勞。

translations.literal: When the Torghuts submitted, he was ordered to proceed to Qiqihar to reward them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Torghuts came in, he was sent to Qiqihar to distribute rewards.

sentences.zh: 授四川總督，未行，仍調授陝甘。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor-general of Sichuan; before departing he was again transferred to Shaanxi-Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Named governor-general of Sichuan, he was reassigned to Shaanxi-Gansu before he could leave.

sentences.zh: 師徵金川，奏陝、甘發兵三千，延綏鎮總兵書明阿以千人赴維州，興漢總兵張大經以二千人入四川從征，文綬如鞏昌、安定視師行。

translations.literal: When the army campaigned against Jinchuan, he memorialized that Shaanxi and Gansu would dispatch three thousand troops: Yan'sui Regional Commander Shu Ming'a would lead one thousand to Weizhou, and Xinghan Regional Commander Zhang Dajing would lead two thousand into Sichuan for the campaign; Wen Shou went to Gongchang and Anding to oversee the army's march.
translations.idiomatic: For the Jinchuan campaign he sent three thousand men from Shaanxi-Gansu—Shu Ming'a with one thousand to Weizhou and Zhang Dajing with two thousand into Sichuan—while he supervised the march from Gongchang and Anding.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，疏言：「巴里坤、烏魯木齊年來日繁盛。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he memorialized: "Barkol and Urumqi have grown more populous year by year.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he reported that Barkol and Urumqi had grown steadily more populous.

sentences.zh: 招民墾地，戶給三十畝，並農具籽種，視新疆例，六年昇科。

translations.literal: He proposed recruiting settlers to open land, granting thirty mu per household together with farm tools and seed, following the Xinjiang precedent of levying tax after six years.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed recruiting settlers, granting thirty mu per household with tools and seed, and taxing after six years as in Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 瑪納斯城南可二萬餘畝，瑚圖璧城西北可六千餘畝，巴里坤城外及傍近諸地五千九百餘畝，玉門、酒泉、敦煌三縣可五千餘畝。

translations.literal: South of Manas city about twenty thousand mu were available; northwest of Hutubi city about six thousand mu; outside Barkol and nearby places about five thousand nine hundred mu; in Yumen, Jiuquan, and Dunhuang counties about five thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: He identified roughly twenty thousand mu south of Manas, six thousand northwest of Hutubi, five thousand nine hundred near Barkol, and five thousand in Yumen, Jiuquan, and Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 往時嘉峪關恆閉，過者候譏察，今關外已同內地，請令辰開酉閉；

translations.literal: Formerly Jiayu Pass was always closed and travelers waited for inspection; now the lands beyond the pass are like the interior; he requested that it open at the chen hour and close at the you hour;
translations.idiomatic: He noted that Jiayu Pass had once been shut tight while travelers waited for inspection, but that the frontier was now like the interior, and asked that it open at dawn and close at dusk;

sentences.zh: 兼開烏魯木齊城南七達色巴山梁以利行旅。」

translations.literal: and also that the Qidasiba pass south of Urumqi be opened to benefit travelers."
translations.idiomatic: and that the Qidasiba ridge south of Urumqi be opened for travelers.

sentences.zh: 又酌定收捐監糧，籌備巴里坤移駐滿洲兵糧料；

translations.literal: He also worked out collection of grain donated for the supervision student title to prepare rations for Manchu troops to be moved to Barkol;
translations.idiomatic: He also arranged grain donations for the student-supervision title to provision Manchu troops relocating to Barkol;

sentences.zh: 並於巴里坤山灣設廠牧羊，令滿洲兵子弟取乳剪毛，以廣生計。

translations.literal: and established a sheep ranch in a Barkol mountain bay so that Manchu soldiers' sons could milk and shear wool to broaden their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: and set up a sheep ranch in a Barkol valley where Manchu soldiers' sons could milk and shear wool for extra income.

sentences.zh: 均如所請行。

translations.literal: All were approved as requested.
translations.idiomatic: All was approved as he asked.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，調四川總督。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was transferred to be governor-general of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he was transferred to governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 前政阿爾泰坐誤軍興，又縱其子明德布婪索，得罪，上命文綬察明德布婪索狀。

translations.literal: His predecessor A'ertai was punished for mishandling the war effort and for indulging his son Mingdebu in extortion; the Emperor ordered Wen Shou to investigate Mingdebu's extortion.
translations.idiomatic: Predecessor A'ertai had been punished for mismanaging the war and indulging Mingdebu's extortion; Wen Shou was told to investigate Mingdebu.

sentences.zh: 文綬言：「明德布侍阿爾泰日久，與屬吏往還，尚無婪索事。」

translations.literal: Wen Shou said: "Mingdebu has long attended A'ertai and has dealings with subordinate officials, but there is no matter of extortion."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Shou reported that Mingdebu, long at A'ertai's side, dealt with subordinates but had not extorted.

sentences.zh: 而明德佈在京師，上命軍機大臣按鞫，具服，乃責文綬袒護，奪官，往伊犁效力。

translations.literal: But Mingdebu was in the capital; the Emperor ordered the Grand Council to investigate and interrogate; he confessed fully; Wen Shou was then blamed for shielding him, stripped of office, and sent to serve at Yili.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdebu in Beijing confessed under Grand Council interrogation; Wen Shou was blamed for shielding him, dismissed, and sent to Yili.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，木果木師潰，總督富勒渾奏報金川酋攻明郭宗河口，上授文綬頭等侍衛，佐富勒渾治軍。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, when the army was routed at Mugongmu, Governor-General Fu Leihun memorialized that the Jinchuan chieftain was attacking the Mingguozong river mouth; the Emperor appointed Wen Shou a first-class bodyguard to assist Fu Leihun in managing the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year, after Mugongmu, Fu Leihun reported Jinchuan attacks on the Mingguozong river mouth; Wen Shou was made a first-class bodyguard to assist him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授湖廣總督，仍署四川總督。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed governor-general of Huguang, still acting as governor-general of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was governor-general of Huguang while still acting in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 偕富勒渾奏言：「增兵需餉，請令商民原自湖廣運糧入四川者，視乾隆十三年范毓馪助餉加銜例，穀一石當銀九錢，授以貢監職銜。」

translations.literal: Together with Fu Leihun he memorialized: "Increased troops require increased pay; merchants who originally transported grain from Huguang into Sichuan should, following the precedent of Fan Yuxi's grain donation in the thirteenth year of Qianlong that earned an honorary title, receive nine cash of silver per picul of grain and be granted the rank of tribute student or supervision student."
translations.idiomatic: With Fu Leihun he proposed that Huguang merchants who hauled grain into Sichuan be paid nine cash of silver per picul and given tribute or supervision student rank, following Fan Yuxi's thirteenth-year precedent.

sentences.zh: 並議行。

translations.literal: It was also approved for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The court also approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，實授。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he was appointed in full.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year he received full appointment.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，入覲。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he attended court.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year he presented himself at court.

sentences.zh: 子國泰，官山東巡撫，召詣京師相見。

translations.literal: His son Guotai served as governor of Shandong and was summoned to the capital to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guotai, governor of Shandong, was called to the capital to see him.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，疏言：「雲南昭通、東川諸屬改食川鹽，應於川、滇交界隘口設稽察。」

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he memorialized: "The subordinate districts of Zhaotong and Dongchuan in Yunnan have been switched to Sichuan salt; inspection posts should be set at passes on the Sichuan-Yunnan border."
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he urged inspection posts on the Sichuan-Yunnan border where Yunnan districts had been switched to Sichuan salt.

sentences.zh: 上可其奏，並諭雲貴總督福康安一律嚴防。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his memorial and also instructed Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Fukang'an to enforce strict precautions uniformly.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved and told Governor-General Fukang'an to tighten controls throughout.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，詔停打箭爐收稅部員，由總督委員管理，因條奏裁改諸事，從之。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year an edict halted the Ministry tax collectors at Dajianlu; management was delegated to the governor-general's commissioners, and his detailed memorial proposing cuts and reforms was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year Dajianlu tax collectors from the Ministry were withdrawn in favor of gubernatorial commissioners, and his reform memorial was adopted.

sentences.zh: 四川多​​盜，民間號啯嚕子，闌入鄰近諸省。

translations.literal: Sichuan had many bandits, whom the people called guluzi; they crossed into neighboring provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits called guluzi were rife in Sichuan and spilled into neighboring provinces.

sentences.zh: 湖廣總督舒常、湖南巡撫劉墉、貴州巡撫李本先後疏言盜自四川入境，遣將吏捕治。

translations.literal: Huguang Governor-General Shu Chang, Hunan Governor Liu Yong, and Guizhou Governor Li Ben successively memorialized that bandits were entering from Sichuan and dispatched officers to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: Governors-general and governors of Huguang, Hunan, and Guizhou reported Sichuan bandits crossing their borders and sent officers after them.

sentences.zh: 文綬奏後入，上責其玩縱，降三品頂帶。

translations.literal: Wen Shou's memorial arrived later; the Emperor blamed his lax indulgence and reduced his rank insignia to third grade.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Shou's report came late; the Emperor faulted his negligence and cut his insignia to third grade.

sentences.zh: 尚書周煌复陳盜為民害，將吏置不問，甚或州縣吏胥身為盜擾民，上以文綬因循貽患，奪官，往伊犁效力。

translations.literal: Minister Zhou Huang again stated that bandits harmed the people while officers ignored them, and that some prefectural and county clerks were themselves bandits harassing the people; the Emperor held that Wen Shou's procrastination had caused the harm, stripped him of office, and sent him to serve at Yili.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhou Huang added that officials ignored banditry and some clerks were bandits themselves; Wen Shou was dismissed for letting the problem fester and sent to Yili.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，釋回。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he was released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year he was pardoned and returned.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the forty-ninth year.

sentences.zh: 子國泰，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Guotai has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guotai is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 劉秉恬，字德引，山西洪洞人。

translations.literal: Liu Bingtian, courtesy name Deyin, a native of Hongdong in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bingtian, styled Deyin, was from Hongdong in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十一年舉人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of the Qianlong reign he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a provincial graduate in the twenty-first year of Qianlong.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，明通榜，授內閣中書，充軍機處章京。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, on the supplemental list, he was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat and served as a clerk in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he entered the Grand Secretariat on the supplemental list and served as a Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 再遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to director.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，考選福建道御史，轉吏科給事中。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was selected censor of the Fujian Circuit and transferred to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he became Fujian Circuit censor, then supervising secretary in the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 大學士傅恆督師討緬甸，以秉恬從，擢鴻臚寺少卿。

translations.literal: When Grand Secretary Fu Heng commanded the army against Burma, Bingtian accompanied him and was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Heng led the Burma campaign, Bingtian went with him and was made vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 師還，超擢左副都御史。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was promoted by exception to left vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he was exceptionally promoted left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部侍郎，調工部，再調倉場。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of Punishments, then to Works, and again to the grain depots.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to vice minister of Punishments, then Works, then the grain depots.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，師徵金川，大學士溫福出西路，總督桂林出南路，授秉恬欽差大臣，督西路糧運。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, when the army campaigned against Jinchuan, Grand Secretary Wen Fu took the western route and Governor-General Guilin the southern route; Bingtian was appointed imperial commissioner to supervise grain transport on the western route.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year Wen Fu took the western route and Guilin the southern route against Jinchuan; Bingtian was made imperial commissioner for western-route grain.

sentences.zh: 尋以南路徑僻站長，輓運尤艱，命改赴南路。

translations.literal: Soon, because the southern route was remote with long stages and transport especially difficult, he was ordered to shift to the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: The southern route's long stages made transport harder, and he was soon ordered to shift there.

sentences.zh: 秉恬以西路需餉急，請暫留料理，上韙之。

translations.literal: Bingtian, because the western route urgently needed supplies, requested to remain temporarily to handle matters; the Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Bingtian asked to stay on the western route where supplies were urgent, and the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「南路運糧，人俱畏其難。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Transporting grain on the southern route—everyone fears the difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote that everyone dreaded the southern route's grain haul.

sentences.zh: 臣非敢言易，然天下無必不可辦之事。」

translations.literal: Your servant does not dare say it is easy, yet under heaven there is nothing that absolutely cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: I do not call it easy, but nothing under heaven is utterly impossible."

sentences.zh: 上諭令勉為之。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed him to exert himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told him to press on.

sentences.zh: 尋奏：「師自甲爾木進攻小金川，道路險阻，唯羊可陟。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized: "The army advancing on Lesser Jinchuan from A'ermu found the roads perilous; only sheep could climb them.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reported that from A'ermu only sheep could traverse the steep paths to Lesser Jinchuan.

sentences.zh: 乃招蠻民販羊至軍，以六羊當米一石。」

translations.literal: He recruited barbarian traders to bring sheep to the army, valuing six sheep as one picul of rice."
translations.idiomatic: He hired frontier traders to drive sheep to camp at six sheep per picul of rice.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「師攻克僧格宗，距達烏圍六十餘裡。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "The army took Senggezong, more than sixty li from Dawuwei.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that Senggezong, taken by the army, lay sixty li from Dawuwei.

sentences.zh: 臣往勘，擬於策爾丹色木設站。

translations.literal: Your servant went to survey and proposes establishing a station at Ca'erdansemu.
translations.idiomatic: He surveyed and proposed a station at Ca'erdansemu.

sentences.zh: 其地有喇嘛寺，糧至即貯寺，以蔽風雨。」

translations.literal: There is a lamasery on the spot; grain arriving would be stored in the temple to shelter it from wind and rain."
translations.idiomatic: Grain would be stored in a lamasery there against wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 旋赴美諾督運。

translations.literal: Soon he went to Meinuo to supervise transport.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Meinuo to supervise transport.

sentences.zh: 上嘉秉恬不辭勞瘁，賜孔雀翎，授四川總督，仍留美諾督運。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised Bingtian for not shirking hardship, granted him a peacock feather, appointed him governor-general of Sichuan, and still left him at Meinuo to supervise transport.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised his endurance, gave him a peacock feather, made him governor-general of Sichuan, and kept him at Meinuo supervising grain.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，師克小金川，溫福督兵進攻昔嶺。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year the army took Lesser Jinchuan, and Wen Fu led troops to attack Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year Lesser Jinchuan fell and Wen Fu advanced on Xiling.

sentences.zh: 上命秉恬將美臥溝、曾頭溝兩路酌量形勢，分別駐守，赴木果木及功噶爾拉兩地察勘。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Bingtian to assess the terrain and garrison separately the Meiwogou and Zengtougou routes, and to go to Mugongmu and Gongga'erla to survey.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered him to garrison Meiwogou and Zengtougou as terrain dictated and to survey Mugongmu and Gongga'erla.

sentences.zh: 秉恬奏至，與上諭正合，深嘉之，諭謂：「勤勞軍務，與統兵督戰無異。

translations.literal: When Bingtian's memorial arrived it matched the imperial instruction exactly; the Emperor deeply praised him and said: "Laboring in military affairs is no different from commanding troops in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His report matched the imperial plan; the Emperor praised him for toiling in logistics as if in battle.

sentences.zh: 命交部照軍功議敘。」

translations.literal: He ordered the ministry to deliberate rewards according to military merit."
translations.idiomatic: Rewards were ordered deliberated on military merit.

sentences.zh: 秉恬途中得綽斯甲布土司遣頭人投禀，訐綽斯甲布與金川親暱，雖從征未嘗盡力，並請歸金川所侵噶爾瑪六宗諸地。

translations.literal: On the road Bingtian received a petition from a headman sent by the Zhuosijia Bu chieftain, accusing Zhuosijia Bu of intimacy with Jinchuan, of not exerting himself in the campaign though following the army, and asking return of the six districts of Ga'erma seized by Jinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: En route a Zhuosijia Bu headman accused his chieftain of favoring Jinchuan, shirking the campaign, and demanded return of seized Ga'erma districts.

sentences.zh: 秉恬諭：「師討金川，斷不中止。

translations.literal: Bingtian instructed: "The army's punitive expedition against Jinchuan will certainly not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Bingtian replied that the campaign against Jinchuan would not halt.

sentences.zh: 噶爾瑪六宗諸地，事平後當有公斷。

translations.literal: The six districts of Ga'erma and other places will receive fair adjudication after the affair is settled.
translations.idiomatic: Ga'erma and the rest would be adjudicated after peace.

sentences.zh: 爾土司從征未得一地，且縱金川人在境內為盜，所謂盡力者安在？」

translations.literal: Your chieftain has gained not a single foot in the campaign, yet allows Jinchuan men to rob within your borders—where is this so-called exertion?"
translations.idiomatic: You gained no ground yet let Jinchuan raiders operate in your territory—where is your exertion?"

sentences.zh: 頭人語塞，奉檄而去。

translations.literal: The headman was speechless and withdrew on receiving the dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: The headman withdrew, unable to answer.

sentences.zh: 疏聞，上嘉秉恬甚合機宜。

translations.literal: When this was reported, the Emperor praised Bingtian as very apt to the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor commended Bingtian's handling as apt.

sentences.zh: 秉恬至木果木，復奏：「臣自崇德抵功噶爾拉，地氣極寒，四山皆雪，甫經設站，以篾席支棚，使人畜暫有棲止。

translations.literal: At Mugongmu Bingtian memorialized again: "From Chongde to Gongga'erla the air is extremely cold and snow covers the four mountains; stations have just been set up with bamboo-mat sheds so men and animals may have temporary shelter.
translations.idiomatic: At Mugongmu he reported bitter cold and snow from Chongde to Gongga'erla and bamboo sheds for men and beasts.

sentences.zh: 至簇拉角克為布朗郭宗運糧要道，兩口東西相距六七十里，開修土路，通至木波，即合帛噶爾角克碉及布朗郭宗大道。

translations.literal: At Culajiaoke, a vital route for grain to Bulangguozong, the two passes east and west are sixty or seventy li apart; an earth road is being opened through to Mubo, joining the Bo'ega'erjiaoke fort and the Bulangguozong highway.
translations.idiomatic: He opened an earth road at Culajiaoke, the Bulangguozong grain route, linking Mubo to the main highway.

sentences.zh: 又自功噶爾拉至木果木，路陡雪滑，已飭修路鑿冰，不致少誤糧道。」

translations.literal: From Gongga'erla to Mugongmu the road is steep and slippery with snow; orders have been issued to repair the road and cut ice so the grain route will not be delayed."
translations.idiomatic: Steep snowy tracks to Mugongmu were being cleared so grain would not lag.

sentences.zh: 報聞，加太子少保。

translations.literal: When this was reported, he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent on report.

sentences.zh: 木果木師潰，以提督董天弼失守底木達、布朗郭宗責秉恬不先奏劾，奪官，予按察使銜留軍。

translations.literal: When the army was routed at Mugongmu, Regional Commander Dong Tianbi was blamed for losing Dimuda and Bulangguozong; Bingtian was blamed for not having impeached him first, stripped of office, and given the rank of surveillance commissioner to remain with the army.
translations.idiomatic: After Mugongmu, Dong Tianbi was blamed for losing Dimuda and Bulangguozong; Bingtian lost office for not impeaching him sooner but stayed with the army as surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 旋並削銜，命佐按察使郝碩督西路運糧。

translations.literal: Soon that rank was also removed, and he was ordered to assist Surveillance Commissioner Hao Shuo in supervising western-route grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: His commissioner's rank was soon stripped too, and he assisted Hao Shuo on western-route grain.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，奏面視米易取攜，已由四川採辦十數万斤；

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he memorialized that face-viewed rice was easy to carry and that more than a hundred thousand jin had already been procured in Sichuan;
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year he reported over a hundred thousand jin of portable husked rice procured in Sichuan;

sentences.zh: 又奏修整楸坻至日爾拉薩拉驛道，並與總督富勒渾議以北路軍餉歸西路遞運：上並嘉納。

translations.literal: He also memorialized repairing the courier road from Qiudi to Rierlasala and, with Governor-General Fu Leihun, proposed relaying northern-route army grain by the western route: the Emperor praised both.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the Qiudi–Rierlasala road and with Fu Leihun relayed northern grain via the western route—all praised.

sentences.zh: 四十年，以督運無誤，授兵部郎中，仍賜孔雀翎，以欽差關防督餉。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year, for error-free supervision of transport, he was appointed director in the Ministry of War, again granted a peacock feather, and given an imperial commissioner's seal to supervise provisions.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year, for flawless transport, he became a War Ministry director with a peacock feather and commissioner's seal.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to vice minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon vice minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以母病召還京師，旋丁憂。

translations.literal: Because his mother was ill he was recalled to the capital, and soon entered mourning.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's illness recalled him to the capital, and he soon entered mourning.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起署陝西巡撫。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to serve as acting governor of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to act as governor of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，召入覲，調署雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was summoned to audience and transferred to act as governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he attended court and was shifted to act as governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，署雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year he served as acting governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year he acted as governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 安南國王以內地人民出邊居住，脅制土民欠稅，且動稱內地差委，徵索租賦，大為民擾，諮請防禁。

translations.literal: The king of Annam reported that people from the interior living beyond the border were coercing native subjects over unpaid taxes, often claiming to be interior dispatch agents collecting rent and levies, greatly harassing the people, and asked that this be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Annam's king complained that Chinese beyond the border extorted native taxes posing as imperial agents, and sought prohibition.

sentences.zh: 秉恬擬照會，略謂：「內地百姓緣爾國需用貨物，特准開關通市，為爾國利賴。

translations.literal: Bingtian drafted a note, in substance: "Interior commoners, because your country needs goods, have been specially allowed to open trade at the passes for your country's benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Bingtian drafted a note saying Chinese traded at the passes for Annam's benefit.

sentences.zh: 本非在外墾田種地，無應納租賦，焉有脅制土民欠稅之理？

translations.literal: They are not reclaiming fields and planting abroad; there is no rent to pay—how can there be reason to coerce native subjects over unpaid taxes?
translations.idiomatic: They do not farm abroad and owe no rent—how can they coerce your subjects?

sentences.zh: 如滋生事端，惟有責令爾國察出送回內地究治。」

translations.literal: If trouble arises, your country alone must investigate, send offenders back to the interior, and punish them."
translations.idiomatic: If trouble arises, Annam must send offenders back for punishment."

sentences.zh: 奏聞，上嘉其得體，仍令軍機大臣刪改，寄秉恬具答。

translations.literal: When this was reported, the Emperor praised its propriety but still ordered the Grand Council to revise it and send it to Bingtian for the reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised the tone but had the Grand Council revise the reply.

sentences.zh: 累年以運銅妥速，議敘。

translations.literal: For successive years of swift, safe copper transport, rewards were deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: Years of reliable copper transport earned merit rewards.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，召授兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he was summoned and appointed vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year he was recalled as vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，調倉場。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he was transferred to the grain depots.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year he took charge of the grain depots.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，復調兵部。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he was again transferred to War.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4 he returned to the War Ministry.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 查禮，字恂叔，順天宛平人。

translations.literal: Cha Li, courtesy name Xunshu, a native of Wanping in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Cha Li, styled Xunshu, was from Wanping in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 少劬學。

translations.literal: In youth he studied diligently.
translations.idiomatic: He studied hard from youth.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，應博學鴻詞科，報罷。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Qianlong reign he entered the special erudite examination and was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 he failed the special erudite examination.

sentences.zh: 入貲授戶部主事，揀發廣西，補慶遠同知。

translations.literal: He purchased office and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, was selected for Guangxi, and was made subprefect of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He bought office as a Revenue clerk, was sent to Guangxi, and became subprefect of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 舉卓異，上命督撫舉堪任知府者。

translations.literal: Rated outstanding, he was ordered that governors and governors-general recommend those fit for prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Rated outstanding, he was put on the list for prefectural promotion.

sentences.zh: 巡撫定長、李錫秦先後以禮薦。

translations.literal: Governors Ding Chang and Li Xiqin successively recommended Li.
translations.idiomatic: Governors Ding Chang and Li Xiqin both recommended him.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢太平知府，母憂去。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted prefect of Taiping and left on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he became prefect of Taiping, then left for mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補四川寧遠。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed to Ningyuan in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was posted to Ningyuan in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，擢川北道。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was promoted intendant of North Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he became North Sichuan intendant.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，調松茂道，

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was transferred to the Song-Mao Circuit,
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he was moved to the Song-Mao Circuit,

sentences.zh: 小金川用兵，總督阿爾泰檄禮治餉；

translations.literal: When Lesser Jinchuan was at war, Governor-General A'ertai ordered Li to manage provisions;
translations.idiomatic: When Lesser Jinchuan was fought, A'ertai put Li in charge of supplies;

sentences.zh: 將軍溫福師進巴朗阿，大營以禮從，令修建汶川桃關索橋，踰月工竟，上嘉之，命專司督運西路糧餉。

translations.literal: General Wen Fu's army advanced to Balang'a with Li accompanying the main camp; he was ordered to build the rope bridge at Taoguan in Wenchuan, which was completed in a month; the Emperor praised this and ordered him to specialize in supervising western-route grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: With Wen Fu at Balang'a Li built Wenchuan's Taoguan rope bridge in a month, won praise, and took western-route grain.

sentences.zh: 三雜穀土司為小金川煽惑，頗懷疑懼。

translations.literal: The three Zagu chieftains, stirred up by Lesser Jinchuan, were quite suspicious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: The three Zagu chieftains, swayed by Lesser Jinchuan, grew fearful.

sentences.zh: 禮諭以利害，眾感服。

translations.literal: Li instructed them on advantage and harm, and the multitude submitted in gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Li explained costs and benefits until they submitted.

sentences.zh: 時溫福出雜穀腦，遣提督董天弼分兵自間道出曾頭溝。

translations.literal: At that time Wen Fu went out through Zagunao and sent Regional Commander Dong Tianbi to divide troops by a secret route out through Zengtougou.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Fu marched through Zagunao while Dong Tianbi took a secret route via Zengtougou.

sentences.zh: 軍需局以儲米半運雜穀腦，曾頭溝軍糧不足，禮坐奪官，仍留軍效力。

translations.literal: The commissariat sent half the stored rice to Zagunao, leaving Zengtougou short of army grain; Li was stripped of office but kept with the army.
translations.idiomatic: Half the rice went to Zagunao, starving Zengtougou; Li was dismissed but kept with the army.

sentences.zh: 師克美諾，溫福令禮與天弼清察戶口地糧，總兵五福自美諾移軍丹壩。

translations.literal: When the army took Meinuo, Wen Fu ordered Li and Tianbi to check household registers and land tax; Regional Commander Wufu moved his army from Meinuo to Danba.
translations.idiomatic: After Meinuo fell, Li and Tianbi tallied households and taxes while Wufu moved to Danba.

sentences.zh: 總督劉秉恬奏禮雖文員，頗強幹，諳番情，命署松茂道，代五福駐美諾撫降番。

translations.literal: Governor-General Liu Bingtian memorialized that though Li was a civil official he was quite capable and understood barbarian conditions; he was ordered to act as Song-Mao intendant, replacing Wufu to garrison Meinuo and pacify surrendered barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Bingtian praised Li's ability and frontier knowledge; he acted as Song-Mao intendant at Meinuo pacifying surrendered tribes.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，木果木師潰，禮偕游擊穆克登阿赴援，至蒙固橋，聞喇嘛寺糧站陷，士卒狼顧；

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, when the army was routed at Mugongmu, Li went with Guerrilla Officer Mukedeng'a to aid; reaching the Menggu Bridge, they heard the lamasery grain station had fallen and the soldiers looked back in panic;
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year, after Mugongmu, Li and Mukedeng'a rushed to the Menggu Bridge and found troops panicking at news the lamasery station had fallen;

sentences.zh: 會鬆茂總兵福昌至，遂復進，遇伏，禮率督兵擊之，擒砦首，餘寇驚遁。

translations.literal: When Song-Mao Regional Commander Fuchang arrived, they advanced again, met an ambush, and Li led supervising troops to attack, capturing a stockade chief while the rest fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchang's arrival steadied them; Li led troops through an ambush, seized a stockade chief, and routed the rest.

sentences.zh: 美諾已陷賊，阿桂馳援，以達圍垂陷，檄禮駐守，尋命真除。

translations.literal: Meinuo had already fallen to the enemy; Agui rushed to aid; as Da was on the verge of encirclement, Li was ordered to garrison there, and soon received regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Meinuo had fallen; Agui relieved Da as it neared collapse; Li garrisoned there and soon received full appointment.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，阿桂師再進，令禮專任臥龍關路糧餉。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, as Agui's army advanced again, Li was ordered to specialize in grain and pay on the Wolongguan route.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year Agui put Li solely in charge of Wolongguan supplies.

sentences.zh: 阿桂秉上旨，以南路陰翳，設疑兵牽綴，奇兵自北山入。

translations.literal: Agui, following the imperial intent, because the southern route was shaded and gloomy, set up decoy troops to pin the enemy while striking with elite troops from the northern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Agui feigned on the gloomy southern route while striking from the northern mountains.

sentences.zh: 禮請自楸坻至薩拉站開日爾拉山，山高五十里，冰雪六七尺，故無行徑。

translations.literal: Li requested opening the Rierla mountain from Qiudi to Sala station; the mountain was fifty li high with six or seven feet of ice and snow, so there had been no path.
translations.idiomatic: Li proposed a road over the fifty-li Rierla ridge from Qiudi to Sala, buried in ice.

sentences.zh: 禮登高相度，以火融積凍，鑿石為磴，不匝月通路二百餘裡。

translations.literal: Li climbed high to survey, melted accumulated ice with fire, cut stone into steps, and in less than a month opened a road of more than two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: He surveyed, melted ice, cut stone steps, and opened two hundred li of road in a month.

sentences.zh: 自楸坻達西北兩路軍​​營，視故道皆近十餘站，省運費月以鉅萬計，特旨嘉獎。

translations.literal: From Qiudi to the northwest and west-route camps, compared with the old roads all were more than ten stations nearer, saving transport costs of tens of thousands per month; an especial edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The new road shortened hauls by ten stations each way, saving tens of thousands a month—earning an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 郭羅克掠蒙古軍牲畜，殺青海公里塔爾，富勒渾令禮及游擊龔學聖捕治，复盜二，還牛馬五百餘，盜渠牛獲。

translations.literal: Guoluoke raiders seized Mongol army livestock and killed Qinghai Prince Gong'erta'er; Fu Leihun ordered Li and Guerrilla Officer Gong Xuesheng to capture them; they again raided twice, returned more than five hundred cattle and horses, and captured the bandit chief Niu Huo.
translations.idiomatic: Guoluoke raiders killed Prince Gong'erta'er; Li and Gong Xuesheng recovered five hundred head and captured chief Niu Huo.

sentences.zh: 富勒渾以禮行後糧運漸遲誤，奏促禮還。

translations.literal: Fu Leihun, because Li's rear grain transport grew gradually late and erroneous, memorialized urging Li to return.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Leihun faulted Li for late rear convoys and urged his recall.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，金川平，禮留辦兵屯，拊循降番，敘功，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, when Jinchuan was pacified, Li remained to manage military colonies and soothe surrendered barbarians; for merit he was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: After the forty-first-year pacification Li stayed to settle military colonies and tribes, earning a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 上遣理籓院郎中阿林、知府倭什布、參將李天貴出黃勝關捕郭羅克盜渠，未得，皆坐奪官；

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Court of Colonial Affairs Director A Lin, Prefect Weshibu, and Regional Commander Li Tiangui out through Huang Shengguan to capture Guoluoke bandit chiefs; they failed and were all stripped of office;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial envoys failed to catch Guoluoke chiefs at Huang Shengguan and were dismissed;

sentences.zh: 仍令禮往捕，禮調三雜穀土兵四千，先令裹糧疾進。

translations.literal: Li was still ordered to go capture them; Li mobilized four thousand Zagu native soldiers and first ordered them to advance swiftly carrying their own rations.
translations.idiomatic: Li was sent again with four thousand Zagu troops ordered forward on their own grain.

sentences.zh: 禮至，宣布上意，郭羅克酋瑪克蘇爾袞布來謁，問盜渠所在，諉不知；

translations.literal: When Li arrived, he announced the imperial will; the Guoluoke chief Maksuer Gunbu came to pay respects; Li asked where the bandit chiefs were, and he pleaded ignorance;
translations.idiomatic: Li arrived bearing the Emperor's message; Guoluoke chief Maksuer Gunbu came to audience but claimed not to know where the bandit leaders were;

sentences.zh: 禮執送內地，責其弟索朗勒爾務捕盜。

translations.literal: Li seized him and sent him to the interior, charging his younger brother Solang Le'er to see to capturing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Li detained him and sent him inland, ordering his brother Solang Le'er to hunt down the robbers.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，瑪克蘇爾袞佈病死，上責禮失撫馭番夷之道。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year, Maksuer Gunbu died of illness; the Emperor blamed Li for failing in the way of governing and controlling tribal peoples.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year of Qianlong Maksuer Gunbu died; the Emperor faulted Li for mishandling frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，擢按察使。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year of Qianlong he was made Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 瞻對番劫里塘熱砦喇嘛寺，禮往按，得盜，寘於法。

translations.literal: Zhandui tribesmen raided the Litang Rezhai Lama temple; Li went to investigate, captured the bandits, and punished them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhandui raiders struck Litang's Rezhai lamasery, Li investigated, caught them, and brought them to justice.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, he was transferred to Financial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year of Qianlong he became Financial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋擢湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon after he was promoted to Governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Hunan Governor.

sentences.zh: 入覲，四十六年，卒於京師。

translations.literal: He entered court audience; in the forty-sixth year he died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After presenting himself at court he died in the capital in year 46.

sentences.zh: 子淳，大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: His son Chun served as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chun rose to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 鄂寶，鄂謨託氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: E Bao was of the Emoto clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: E Bao, an Emoto-clan Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 父西柱，官西安將軍。

translations.literal: His father Xizhu held the post of General of Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xizhu was General of Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 鄂寶自官學生授內閣中書。

translations.literal: E Bao, starting as a student of the Imperial Academy, was appointed a Secretariat Drafter in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: From the Imperial Academy E Bao entered the Grand Secretariat as a drafter.

sentences.zh: 再遷戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Assistant Department Director in the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made an assistant director in the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十六年，授奉天府尹。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Qianlong, he was appointed Intendant of Fengtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 16 he became Intendant of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 二十年，署廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he served as acting Governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Qianlong he acted as Governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，總督李侍堯劾陸川知縣應斯鳴等縱賊害民，鄂寶奏前後相歧，奪官，以三品銜往庫車辦事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, Governor-General Li Shiyao impeached Lucuan Magistrate Ying Siming and others for indulging bandits and harming the people; E Bao memorialized that the earlier and later accounts contradicted each other; he was stripped of office and sent to Kuche to serve affairs with third-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Qianlong Governor-General Li Shiyao accused Lucuan's magistrate of shielding bandits; E Bao's conflicting reports cost him his post, and he was sent to Kuche on third-rank assignment.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，召還，署左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, he was recalled and appointed acting Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled in year 31, he served as acting Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 仍授巡撫，歷湖北、貴州、福建、廣西、山西諸省。

translations.literal: He was again appointed governor, serving successively in Hubei, Guizhou, Fujian, Guangxi, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to provincial governorships in Hubei, Guizhou, Fujian, Guangxi, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 內遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred inward to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the capital as Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 金川用兵，三十七年七月，命侍郎劉秉恬及鄂寶督餉，秉恬主西路，鄂寶及散秩大臣阿爾泰主南路，尋令改主西路。

translations.literal: When troops were deployed in Jinchuan, in the seventh month of the thirty-seventh year, Vice Minister Liu Bingtian and E Bao were ordered to supervise provisions; Bingtian took charge of the western route, E Bao and Minister without Rank A'ertai took charge of the southern route; soon the order was changed so that E Bao took charge of the western route.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinchuan year 37, month 7, Liu Bingtian and E Bao were put in charge of supplies—Bingtian on the west, E Bao and A'ertai on the south, until E Bao was shifted to the west.

sentences.zh: 鄂寶議人負米五斗，日行一站，騾負米石，日行可二三站，改以騾運，軍糈得無缺，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: E Bao proposed that a man carry five dou of rice and march one station per day, while a mule could carry one shi and march two or three stations per day; he changed transport to mules, and army grain suffered no shortage; he was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: E Bao switched convoys to mule transport—one shi per mule, two or three stations a day—and kept the army fed, earning a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，仍授山西巡撫，督餉如故。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, he was again appointed Governor of Shanxi, supervising provisions as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year of Qianlong he resumed as Shanxi Governor while still overseeing supplies.

sentences.zh: 溫福師自功噶爾拉入，阿桂自當噶爾拉入，豐升額自綽斯甲布入。

translations.literal: Wen Fu's army entered by Gongga'erla, Agui's by Dangga'erla, and Feng Sheng'e's by Chuosijiabu.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Fu advanced through Gongga'erla, Agui through Dangga'erla, and Feng Sheng'e through Chuosijiabu.

sentences.zh: 鄂寶駐大板昭主餽溫福軍，秉恬駐底木達主餽阿桂軍；

translations.literal: E Bao was stationed at Daban Zhao to supply Wen Fu's army, and Bingtian was stationed at Dimuda to supply Agui's army;
translations.idiomatic: E Bao fed Wen Fu's force from Daban Zhao while Bingtian fed Agui's from Dimuda;

sentences.zh: 而豐升額軍出綽斯甲布，南路自打箭爐往，秉恬兼任之，西路自三雜穀、丹壩往，鄂寶兼任之。

translations.literal: Feng Sheng'e's army came out through Chuosijiabu; the southern route ran from Dajianlu, which Bingtian also took charge of; the western route ran from Sanzagu and Danba, which E Bao also took charge of.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Sheng'e marched from Chuosijiabu; Bingtian handled the southern line from Dajianlu, E Bao the western line from Sanzagu and Danba.

sentences.zh: 木果木師潰，底木達、大板昭皆陷賊。

translations.literal: When the Muguo wood army collapsed, Dimuda and Daban Zhao both fell to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: After the Muguo wood disaster, Dimuda and Daban Zhao both fell.

sentences.zh: 上命阿桂整兵復進，鄂寶仍駐覺木交督餉。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Agui to reorganize the troops and advance again; E Bao remained stationed at Juemujiao supervising provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Agui was ordered to regroup and push forward; E Bao stayed at Juemujiao to keep supplies moving.

sentences.zh: 旋進翁古爾壟，疏調副將董果護後路。

translations.literal: He soon advanced to Wenggu'erlong and memorialized requesting that Vice Commander Dong Guo protect the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Wenggu'erlong, he asked Vice Commander Dong Guo to secure the rear.

sentences.zh: 上又命原任江西布政使顏希深馳驛往佐之。

translations.literal: The Emperor also ordered former Jiangxi Financial Commissioner Yan Xishen to hurry by courier post to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also sent former Jiangxi Financial Commissioner Yan Xishen posthaste to assist.

sentences.zh: 副將軍明亮等又請令鄂寶駐丹東，上念鄂寶兵少，命以湖廣續調兵千人屬鄂寶。

translations.literal: Deputy General Mingliang and others again requested that E Bao be stationed at Dandong; the Emperor, mindful that E Bao had few troops, ordered that one thousand additional troops recently transferred from Huguang be placed under E Bao.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingliang asked E Bao to hold Dandong, the Emperor added a thousand Huguang reinforcements to his small command.

sentences.zh: 阿桂又疏請桂林率李世傑主南路，令鄂寶主西路。

translations.literal: Agui again memorialized requesting that Guilin lead Li Shijie in charge of the southern route and that E Bao take charge of the western route.
translations.idiomatic: Agui proposed Guilin and Li Shijie for the south and E Bao for the west.

sentences.zh: 丹壩至綽斯甲布糧運，鄂寶請以丹東屬桂林兼領。

translations.literal: For grain transport from Danba to Chuosijiabu, E Bao requested that Dandong be placed under Guilin's joint command.
translations.idiomatic: E Bao asked Guilin to take Dandong as well for the Danba–Chuosijiabu grain route.

sentences.zh: 旋詣丹壩置台站，副將軍豐升額自凱立葉進兵。

translations.literal: He soon went to Danba to establish relay stations; Deputy General Feng Sheng'e advanced troops from Kailiye.
translations.idiomatic: He set up relay stations at Danba while Feng Sheng'e advanced from Kailiye.

sentences.zh: 鄂寶請自三雜穀、梭磨、卓克採轉輸凱立葉，較丹壩道為近。

translations.literal: E Bao requested transshipment from Sanzagu, Suomo, and Zhuokecai to Kailiye, which was nearer than the Danba route.
translations.idiomatic: E Bao proposed routing supplies through Sanzagu, Suomo, and Zhuokecai to Kailiye—a shorter haul than via Danba.

sentences.zh: 豐升額進攻谷噶，鄂寶請自梭落柏古轉輸色木多，凱立葉留少兵，即裁站夫，省糜費。

translations.literal: When Feng Sheng'e attacked Guga, E Bao requested transshipment from Suoluobogu to Semuduo, leaving few troops at Kailiye and immediately cutting relay laborers to save waste.
translations.idiomatic: During Feng Sheng'e's assault on Guga, E Bao rerouted supplies from Suoluobogu to Semuduo and trimmed relay crews at Kailiye to cut costs.

sentences.zh: 會明亮自宜喜進兵，既克達爾圖，兩路軍合師沙壩，克勒烏圍。

translations.literal: When Mingliang advanced from Yixi and had captured Da'ertu, the two armies joined at Shaba and captured Lewuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Mingliang's advance from Yixi took Da'ertu; the two columns united at Shaba and seized Lewuwei.

sentences.zh: 鄂寶請將西路台站以次裁撤。

translations.literal: E Bao requested that the western-route relay stations be dismantled in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: E Bao asked to shut down the western relay stations one by one.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，金川平，軍功加一級。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, when Jinchuan was pacified, he was granted one grade of military merit.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinchuan's pacification in year 41 he received a grade of military merit.

sentences.zh: 七月，調湖南巡撫，仍留辦軍需奏銷。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, he was transferred to Governor of Hunan, still remaining to handle military supply accounts.
translations.idiomatic: In month 7 he became Hunan Governor but stayed on to settle supply accounts.

sentences.zh: 十月，授漕運總督。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he was appointed Director-General of Grain Transport.
translations.idiomatic: In month 10 he was made Director-General of Grain Transport.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，大學士於敏中等議報銷四川軍需不符，請令鄂寶等分償，得旨豁免。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, Grand Secretary Yu Minzhong and others deliberated reporting that Sichuan military supply accounts did not match and requested that E Bao and others share compensation; an edict granted exemption.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year of Qianlong Yu Minzhong found Sichuan supply accounts short; E Bao and others were ordered to make good the deficit, but the Emperor waived it.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，授盛京戶部侍郎，兼奉天府府尹。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year, he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue at Mukden, concurrently serving as Intendant of Fengtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year of Qianlong he became Mukden Vice Minister of Revenue and Fengtian Intendant.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 52.

sentences.zh: 子文通，官內閣侍讀學士，兼公中佐領。

translations.literal: His son Wentong served as Secretariat Reader and concurrently as a company commander in the imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wentong was a Secretariat Reader and imperial guard company commander.

sentences.zh: 顏希深，字若愚，廣東連平州人。

translations.literal: Yan Xishen, styled Ruoyu, was a native of Lianping Prefecture, Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xishen (Ruoyu) came from Lianping, Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 入貲授山西太原同知。

translations.literal: By purchase of office he was appointed Subprefect of Taiyuan, Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He bought office as Subprefect of Taiyuan, Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 累遷山東泰安知府。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Prefect of Tai'an, Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts to Prefect of Tai'an, Shandong.

sentences.zh: 建考棚、書院，清察徵漕浮收諸弊。

translations.literal: He built examination halls and academies and thoroughly investigated abuses in grain tax collection and illegal surcharges.
translations.idiomatic: He built exam halls and academies and cleaned up grain-tax graft.

sentences.zh: 高宗東巡，召對，褒以「他時可大用」。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor toured the east, he was summoned for audience and praised with the words, "He may be greatly employed in the future."
translations.idiomatic: Summoned during the eastern tour, he was told he would be "greatly employed hereafter."

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十七年，授四川按察使，入覲，上以希深母老，尚欲隨任，希深亦不敢奏請改補近地，母子知大義，命調希深江西。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Qianlong, he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan; upon entering audience, because Xishen's mother was old and still wished to accompany him to his post, and Xishen also dared not memorialize requesting reassignment to a nearer place, the Emperor said that mother and son understood great principle and ordered Xishen transferred to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 27 he became Sichuan Surveillance Commissioner; the Emperor, moved that he and his aged mother would not ask for a nearer post, transferred him to Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，遷福建布政使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he was transferred to Financial Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of Qianlong he became Fujian Financial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，調江西，丁母憂去。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, he was transferred to Jiangxi and left office upon mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Jiangxi in year 32, he left to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，仍授江西布政使，又丁父憂去。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, he was again appointed Financial Commissioner of Jiangxi and again left upon mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: Reappointed in year 34, he resigned again when his father died.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，詣京師，命赴金川軍佐鄂寶治餉，援河南布政使，仍留軍。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, he went to the capital and was ordered to proceed to the Jinchuan army to assist E Bao in managing provisions; he was granted the rank of Henan Financial Commissioner but still remained with the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year of Qianlong he was sent to Jinchuan to assist E Bao with supplies, with Henan Financial Commissioner rank but remaining at the front.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「糧台設木池，因限於山，與軍營相隔，將山地開平安營。
