translations.literal: He memorialized: "The grain depot was set at Muchi because of mountain constraints and separation from the camp; the mountain ground should be cleared and a level camp established.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that the Muchi depot, cut off from camp by mountains, should be cleared for a proper garrison.

sentences.zh: 臣與黃岩總兵李時擴督兵防護，時令將弁操演，不但技藝熟練，而槍聲遠近相聞，亦可牽綴賊勢。」

translations.literal: Your subject, together with Huangyan Regional Commander Li Shikuo, supervised troops in defense; he regularly ordered officers and men to drill, so that not only were skills practiced, but the sound of muskets heard near and far could also tie down enemy strength.
translations.idiomatic: With Regional Commander Li Shikuo he drilled the garrison so musket fire echoed across the hills and pinned down the enemy.

sentences.zh: 又言：「覺木交深林密箐，賊易以藏身。

translations.literal: He also said: "Juemujiao has deep forests and dense ravines, where bandits easily hide.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that Juemujiao's thick woods gave rebels perfect cover.

sentences.zh: 臣督兵斬伐林木，使附近賊碉有徑可通處，絕無遮蔽，藉免竊發。」

translations.literal: Your subject supervised troops in felling trees so that where enemy forts nearby had paths leading through, there was absolutely no cover, thereby preventing surprise attacks.
translations.idiomatic: He had trees cut around enemy forts to strip away ambush cover.

sentences.zh: 皆稱旨，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: All were approved by the throne, and he was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved both proposals and gave him a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 木池站焚毀火藥，希深請與時擴分償。

translations.literal: When the Muchi station's stored gunpowder was burned and destroyed, Xishen requested to share compensation with Shikuo.
translations.idiomatic: After gunpowder burned at Muchi station, Xishen offered to split damages with Shikuo.

sentences.zh: 師深入，山重雪積，希深催督拊循，恆終夜露宿。

translations.literal: As the army pushed deep in, mountains piled with snow, Xishen urged and comforted the men and often slept in the open all night.
translations.idiomatic: Deep in snowbound mountains he drove and comforted the convoys, often sleeping under the stars.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，擢湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, he was promoted to Governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year of Qianlong he became Hunan Governor.

sentences.zh: 旋入為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon after he entered the capital as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon brought to the capital as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，復出署貴州巡撫，調雲南。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, he again went out to serve as acting Governor of Guizhou and was transferred to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year of Qianlong he acted as Guizhou Governor, then moved to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 徐績，漢軍正藍旗人。

translations.literal: Xu Ji was a Han Chinese bannerman of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ji, a Han bannerman of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十二年舉人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Qianlong he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial exams in Qianlong 12.

sentences.zh: 入貲授山東兗州泉河通判。

translations.literal: By purchase of office he was appointed Subprefect of the Quanhe River at Yanzhou, Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He bought office as Quanhe River subprefect at Yanzhou, Shandong.

sentences.zh: 累遷山東濟東泰武道。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Intendant of Jidong Taiwu Circuit, Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Intendant of Jidong Taiwu Circuit.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，擢按察使，丁父憂，命以按察使銜往哈密辦事，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner; upon mourning for his father, he was ordered to proceed to Hami to handle affairs with Surveillance Commissioner rank and was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Surveillance Commissioner in year 34, he went to Hami on mourning leave with commissioner rank and a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，擢工部侍郎、烏魯木齊辦事大臣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works and Commissioner for Affairs at Urumqi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year of Qianlong he became Vice Minister of Works and Urumqi Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，奏：「瑪納斯在伊犁、塔爾巴哈台之間，請駐兵，使聲勢聯絡。」

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, he memorialized: "Manas lies between Ili and Tarbagatai; troops should be stationed there so that military presence is linked.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong he proposed garrisoning Manas between Ili and Tarbagatai to link the frontier posts.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 授山東巡撫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，上幸天津，迎謁，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, when the Emperor visited Tianjin, Ji went to welcome and pay respects and was granted a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor visited Tianjin in year 38, Ji was given a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，壽張民王倫為亂，績率兵捕治，次臨清城南，為倫所圍，總兵惟一赴援，戰敗。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, the Shouzhang commoner Wang Lun raised rebellion; Ji led troops to capture and suppress him; encamped south of Linqing city, he was surrounded by Lun; Regional Commander Wei Yi went to reinforce and was defeated in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year of Qianlong Wang Lun rebelled at Shouzhang; Ji besieged him south of Linqing until Regional Commander Wei Yi's relief force was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 上遣左都御史阿思哈率兵援績，並令大學士舒赫德視師。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched Left Censor-in-Chief Asiha with troops to reinforce Ji and also ordered Grand Secretary Shuhede to inspect the army.
translations.idiomatic: Asiha was sent with reinforcements and Grand Secretary Shuhede to oversee the campaign.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「績為巡撫，地方有此奸民，不早覺察，不為無罪；

translations.literal: An edict said: "Ji, as governor, bears some guilt for not detecting such wicked commoners in his jurisdiction early;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said Ji was not blameless for failing to spot the trouble early,

sentences.zh: 但以民亂將巡撫治罪，適足長其刁頑，事定，功過自不能掩。」

translations.literal: but to punish a governor because the people rebel would only encourage their obstinacy; when the affair is settled, merit and fault cannot be concealed.
translations.idiomatic: but punishing a governor for a popular revolt would only embolden malcontents—merit and fault would be weighed when order returned.

sentences.zh: 尋事定，命解任，責捕倫餘黨，捕得倫弟柱、林等二十餘人。

translations.literal: Soon the affair was settled; he was ordered relieved of office and charged to capture Lun's remaining followers; he captured Lun's younger brothers Zhu, Lin, and more than twenty others.
translations.idiomatic: When the revolt ended he was removed but told to hunt Lun's allies, capturing Lun's brothers Zhu and Lin and over twenty others.

sentences.zh: 上嘉績黽勉，授河南巡撫，仍繳進孔雀翎示儆。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised Ji's diligence and appointed him Governor of Henan, still requiring him to surrender the peacock feather as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Praising his diligence, the Emperor made him Henan Governor but took back his peacock feather as a warning.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，奏按察使趙銓健忘，上責績於銓應否去留不置一辭，下吏議，奪官，命寬之。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, he memorialized that Surveillance Commissioner Zhao Quan was forgetful; the Emperor blamed Ji for not saying a word on whether Quan should stay or go; the case went to the legal offices for deliberation; he was stripped of office but the Emperor showed leniency.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year of Qianlong he reported Surveillance Commissioner Zhao Quan as forgetful; censured for saying nothing on Quan's fate, he lost his post but was spared.

sentences.zh: 召授禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he became Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，坐雩祭禮器誤，奪官，以三品頂帶往和闐辦事。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year, for error in rain-prayer ritual vessels he was stripped of office and sent to Khotan to handle affairs with third-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year of Qianlong a ritual-vessel error cost him his post; he was sent to Khotan on third rank.

sentences.zh: 召授正黃旗漢軍副都統，遷正紅旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed Vice Commander of the Plain Yellow Han Banner, then transferred to Commander of the Plain Red Han Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he became Plain Yellow Han Banner vice commander, then Plain Red Han Banner commander.

sentences.zh: 六十年，上詢前政弘旴在官事蹟，奏不實，奪官，以六品頂帶往和闐辦事。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year, when the Emperor inquired about the official conduct of his former subordinate Hong Xu, he memorialized untruthfully and was stripped of office and sent to Khotan to handle affairs with sixth-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year of Qianlong he lied about subordinate Hong Xu's record and was demoted to sixth rank at Khotan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，授三等侍衛、烏什辦事大臣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, he was appointed Third-Rank Bodyguard and Commissioner for Affairs at Ush.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1 he became Third-Rank Bodyguard and Ush Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 召授大理寺少卿，還孔雀翎。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and had the peacock feather restored.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, he regained his peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 再遷宗人府府丞。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 十年，以病乞休。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he requested retirement on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Qianlong he retired for illness.

sentences.zh: 十二年，重與鹿鳴宴，賜二品銜。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was again invited to the Deer-Ming banquet and granted second-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Qianlong he attended the Deer-Ming banquet and received second-rank rank.

sentences.zh: 十六年，績子錕，授建寧總兵，入覲，上以績年逾八十，調錕直隸正定總兵，俾就養。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Ji's son Kun was appointed General of Jianning; upon entering audience, because Ji was over eighty, the Emperor transferred Kun to General of Zhengding in Zhili so that he could be near to support his father.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Qianlong his son Kun, made Jianning general, was moved to Zhengding so the eighty-year-old Ji could be near him.

sentences.zh: 卒，錕官至直隸提督。

translations.literal: When Ji died, Kun rose to Governor-General of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: After Ji's death Kun rose to Zhili Governor-General.

sentences.zh: 覺羅圖思德，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Jueluo Tusi De was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Jueluo Tusi De, a Bordered Yellow Banner Manchu.

sentences.zh: 初自諸生授光祿寺筆帖式。

translations.literal: At first, from licentiate status he was appointed a clerk in the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a licentiate clerk in the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Assistant Department Director in the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to assistant director in the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 外授江南常鎮道。

translations.literal: He was sent out to serve as Intendant of Chang-Zhen Circuit in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Jiangnan Chang-Zhen intendant.

sentences.zh: 再遷貴州布政使。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Financial Commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became Guizhou Financial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十七年，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year of Qianlong, he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 37 he was made governor.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「貴州威寧瑪姑柞子廠，水城福集廠產黑、白鉛，歲供京局及各省鼓鑄。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "At the Magu Zhazichang in Weining, Guizhou, and the Fuiji Chang in Shuicheng, black and white lead are produced, supplied yearly to the capital mints and provincial coinages.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that Weining's Magu Zhazichang and Shuicheng's Fuiji Chang produced black and white lead for the capital and provincial mints.

sentences.zh: 廠員營私滯運，請立條款，嚴處分。」

translations.literal: The factory officials engaged in private profit and delayed transport; regulations should be established and strict penalties imposed.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for strict rules and penalties against factory officials who hoarded lead for private gain.

sentences.zh: 並下部議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was also sent to the relevant ministry for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The Board approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，署雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, he served as acting Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year of Qianlong he acted as Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General.

sentences.zh: 上令出駐永昌，並諭以防邊事重，視前政彰寶舊日章程益加奮勉。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered him to proceed to Yongchang and also instructed that frontier defense was weighty and that he should exert himself even more than under his predecessor Zhang Bao's former regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to Yongchang, he was told frontier defense outweighed everything and to exceed Zhang Bao's old standards.

sentences.zh: 抵任後，疏言：「清釐彰寶移交文牘，永昌軍需造銷牽混，應請各歸各款，以清眉目。

translations.literal: After arriving, he memorialized: "Sorting through the documents Zhang Bao transferred, Yongchang military supply accounts are confused and mixed; each item should be kept to its own category to clarify the accounts.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he found Zhang Bao's Yongchang supply accounts tangled and asked that each fund be separated.

sentences.zh: 造解京箭，各鎮協稱現多損壞，與彰寶原奏不符；

translations.literal: Arrows manufactured and forwarded to the capital: each garrison and command reported many damaged now, which did not match Zhang Bao's original memorial;
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons reported far more damaged arrows than Zhang Bao's original figures;

sentences.zh: 又有批准保山等廳縣添買倉穀，亦滋疑義。」

translations.literal: there were also approved purchases of granary grain for Baoshan and other subprefectures and counties, which likewise raised doubts.
translations.idiomatic: approved grain purchases for Baoshan and other districts also looked suspicious.

sentences.zh: 尋劾保山知縣王錫、永平知縣沈文亨侵虧倉穀，請奪官鞫治。

translations.literal: Soon he impeached Baoshan Magistrate Wang Xi and Yongping Magistrate Shen Wenheng for embezzling and depleting granary grain and requested that their offices be stripped and they be tried.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached magistrates Wang Xi of Baoshan and Shen Wenheng of Yongping for granary embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 上命侍郎袁守侗馳驛往按，錫言彰寶勒索供應四萬餘，致虧短兵糧，上震怒，逮彰寶治罪。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Vice Minister Yuan Shoutong to hurry by courier post to investigate; Xi said Zhang Bao had extorted more than forty thousand in supplies, causing shortfalls in soldiers' grain; the Emperor was greatly angered and had Zhang Bao arrested and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Investigator Yuan Shoutong found Wang Xi accusing Zhang Bao of extorting 40,000 in supplies and starving the troops; Zhang Bao was arrested.

sentences.zh: 圖思德以箭二十萬解四川軍營，上嘉之。

translations.literal: Tusi De forwarded two hundred thousand arrows to the Sichuan army camp; the Emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Tusi De sent 200,000 arrows to the Sichuan front and was commended.

sentences.zh: 十一月，兼署雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, he also concurrently served as acting Governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In month 11 he also acted as Yunnan Governor.

sentences.zh: 自傅恆徵緬甸還師，緬甸貢使久不至，閉關絕市年久。

translations.literal: Since Fu Heng's withdrawal from the Burma campaign, Burmese tribute envoys had long failed to arrive, and the border had been closed to trade for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Since Fu Heng withdrew from Burma, tribute missions had ceased and the border had been shut for years.

sentences.zh: 圖思德奏言：「偵知緬民亟盻開關，緬酋亦窘迫有投誠意。

translations.literal: Tusi De memorialized: "Spies report that Burmese people urgently hope for the border to open, and the Burmese chief is also hard pressed and inclined to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He reported Burmese commoners eager for trade and their ruler ready to submit.

sentences.zh: 惟風聞難信，但當簡練軍實，使聞風生畏。」

translations.literal: Only hearsay cannot be trusted; one should simply drill the army and make real preparations so that they will fear at the mere report.
translations.idiomatic: Hearsay was unreliable, he said—better to drill troops until Burma feared China's strength.

sentences.zh: 上韙之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 及兼署巡撫，自永昌還會城，令提督錦山等董理邊防，疏報，怫上意，嚴旨促仍赴永昌督辦邊防。

translations.literal: When he also concurrently served as acting governor, returning from Yongchang to the provincial capital, he ordered Regional Commander Jinshan and others to manage frontier defense and memorialized; this displeased the Emperor, who issued a stern edict urging him to return to Yongchang to supervise frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Yongchang to the capital he reassigned frontier duties—drawing a sharp order to go back to Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，復奏：「偵知緬酋懵駁已死，子贅角牙嗣立，方幼，頭人得魯蘊將遣使叩關納貢。」

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, he again memorialized: "Spies report that the Burmese chief Mengbo is dead; his son Zhuajia'ya has succeeded, still young; the headman Deluyun will send envoys to knock at the border gate and offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of Qianlong he reported Burma's Mengbo dead, a boy on the throne, and headman Deluyun ready to send tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 上以緬甸初無悔罪輸誠之意，諭勿輕聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor, believing Burma at first had no intention of repenting and offering sincerity, instructed that this not be lightly believed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, seeing no sincere repentance, warned against trusting the report.

sentences.zh: 尋奏：「得魯蘊遣使投禀，原送還內地官人，貢象，乞開關。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized: "Deluyun has sent envoys with a petition, originally to return officials detained in the interior, offering elephants in tribute and begging to open the border.
translations.idiomatic: He then reported Deluyun's envoys offering elephants and asking to reopen trade while returning detained officials.

sentences.zh: 已飭龍州將吏與以回文。」

translations.literal: Longzhou officers and officials have already been ordered to reply in writing.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhou officials had already sent a written reply.

sentences.zh: 上以圖思德示緬甸有遷就結案之意，斥為大謬。

translations.literal: The Emperor, believing Tusi De showed an inclination to compromise with Burma and close the case, rebuked this as gross error.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor denounced Tusi De for seeming eager to settle with Burma on easy terms.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，又奏得魯蘊欲將所留楊重英、蘇爾相、多朝相等送還，並叩關納貢。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, he again memorialized that Deluyun wished to return those detained—Yang Chongying, Su Erxiang, Duo Chaoqiang, and others—and also knock at the border gate and offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year of Qianlong he reported Deluyun ready to return Yang Chongying, Su Erxiang, Duo Chaoqiang, and others with tribute.

sentences.zh: 上念受降事重，圖思德不能勝其任，命大學士阿桂赴雲南主持。

translations.literal: The Emperor, mindful that accepting surrender was a weighty matter and that Tusi De could not bear the responsibility, ordered Grand Secretary Agui to proceed to Yunnan to take charge.
translations.idiomatic: Accepting surrender was too weighty for Tusi De; Grand Secretary Agui was sent to Yunnan to take charge.

sentences.zh: 調李侍堯雲貴總督，圖思德回貴州巡撫任。

translations.literal: Li Shiyao was transferred to Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou; Tusi De returned to his post as Governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiyao became governor-general while Tusi De returned to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，擢湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, he was promoted to Governor-General of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year of Qianlong he became Huguang Governor-General.

sentences.zh: 卒，賜祭葬，諡恭愨。

translations.literal: He died; sacrificial rites and burial honors were granted, and he was posthumously titled Gongque.
translations.idiomatic: He died with sacrificial honors and the posthumous title Gongque.

sentences.zh: 彰寶，鄂謨託氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Zhang Bao was of the Emoto clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bao, an Emoto-clan Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年，自繙譯舉人授內閣中書。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong, from translator licentiate he was appointed a Secretariat Drafter in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 13 the translator licentiate entered the Grand Secretariat as a drafter.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授江蘇淮安海防同知。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was appointed Subprefect of Huai'an Coastal Defense, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Qianlong he became Huai'an coastal defense subprefect in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 累遷江寧布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Financial Commissioner of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Jiangning Financial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三十年，授山西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, he was appointed Governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Qianlong he became Shanxi Governor.

sentences.zh: 陽曲知縣段成功虧帑事發，具得巡撫和其衷畀銀五百為彌補及布政使文綬等知情狀，奏聞。

translations.literal: When Yangqu Magistrate Duan Chenggong's treasury deficit came to light, the full facts were obtained that the governor Qihai had agreed in his heart and given five hundred taels of silver as a cover payment, and that Financial Commissioner Wen Shou and others knew of it; this was memorialized to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed Yangqu Magistrate Duan Chenggong's deficit and Governor Qihai's 500-tael hush payment, implicating Financial Commissioner Wen Shou.

sentences.zh: 上遣侍郎四達會鞫得實，其衷、成功論斬，文綬等戍軍台。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched Vice Minister Sida to join in trial and verify the facts; Qihai and Chenggong were sentenced to decapitation, and Wen Shou and others were sent to garrison duty at the military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Sida confirmed the case; Qihai and Chenggong were condemned to death, Wen Shou and others to frontier garrison.

sentences.zh: 安邑知縣馮兆觀揭河東鹽政達色累商及受贄禮、門包，又遣四達會鞫，並得河東運使吳雲從因被四達糾參，嗾兆觀揭發狀，達色論死，雲從、兆觀治罪如律。

translations.literal: Anyi Magistrate Feng Zhaoguan exposed Hedong Salt Controller Dase for oppressing merchants and accepting bribes and door gifts; Sida was again dispatched to join in trial, and it was also found that Hedong Transport Commissioner Wu Yuncong, because he had been impeached by Sida, had incited Zhaoguan to expose him; Dase was sentenced to death, and Yuncong and Zhaoguan were punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Anyi Magistrate Feng Zhaoguan exposed salt controller Dase's graft; the probe also caught Transport Commissioner Wu Yuncong instigating the complaint—Dase was executed, the others punished.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，調江蘇。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, he was transferred to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year of Qianlong he was transferred to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 兩淮鹽政尤拔世奏繳本年提引徵銀，上以此項歷年均未奏明，自乾隆十一年起，應有千餘萬，命彰寶會同詳察。

translations.literal: Liang-Huai Salt Controller You Bash shi memorialized turning in the year's advance levy silver; the Emperor, because this item in successive years had never been clearly memorialized and from the eleventh year of Qianlong there should have been more than ten million, ordered Zhang Bao to join in detailed investigation.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang-Huai salt controller You Bash shi turned in advance levies, the Emperor noted ten million taels unaccounted for since Qianlong 11 and ordered Zhang Bao to investigate.

sentences.zh: 前任鹽政高恆、普福、運使盧見曾均坐是得罪；

translations.literal: Former salt controllers Gao Heng, Pu Fu, and Transport Commissioner Lu Jianzeng were all punished for this;
translations.idiomatic: Former controllers Gao Heng, Pu Fu, and Transport Commissioner Lu Jianzeng all fell in the probe;

sentences.zh: 又發前任監掣同知楊守英詐取商銀：並論如律。

translations.literal: it was also discovered that former Supervisory Controller Subprefect Yang Shouying had fraudulently taken merchants' silver: all were punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: as did former supervisory subprefect Yang Shouying for extorting merchants.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，命馳驛往雲南署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, he was ordered to hurry by courier post to Yunnan to serve as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year of Qianlong he was rushed to Yunnan as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 師徵緬甸，署雲貴總督，命出駐老官屯督餉，加太子太保。

translations.literal: When the army campaigned against Burma, he served as acting Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou, was ordered to proceed to Laoguantun to supervise provisions, and was granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Burma campaign he acted as governor-general from Laoguantun with Grand Guardian rank.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，奏：「永昌沿邊千餘裡，山深徑僻，應於曩宋關、緬箐山、隴川、龍陵、姚關及順寧篾笆橋設卡駐兵。」

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, he memorialized: "Along more than a thousand li of Yongchang's frontier, where mountains are deep and paths remote, checkpoints and garrison troops should be set at Nangsong Pass, Miankeng Mountain, Longchuan, Longling, Yao Pass, and the Bamboo-Bridge at Shunning.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year of Qianlong he proposed garrison checkpoints along Yongchang's thousand-li mountain frontier at Nangsong, Miankeng, Longchuan, Longling, Yao Pass, and Shunning's Bamboo-Bridge.

sentences.zh: 上令實力督率。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered him to supervise and lead in earnest.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered him to enforce this in earnest.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「貴州調至兵間有老弱，現加甄汰。」

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Among troops transferred from Guizhou there are some old and weak; they are now being screened and eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: He reported weeding out old and weak troops transferred from Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 上責：「彰寶現為總督，兩省皆所轄，何不劾奏？」

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked him: "Zhang Bao is now governor-general; both provinces are under his jurisdiction—why did he not impeach and memorialized?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked him for not impeaching bad troops when both provinces were his.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，劾雲南巡撫諾木親才識不能勝任，召還；

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, he impeached Yunnan Governor Nuomuqin as lacking talent and capacity for the post; Nuomuqin was recalled;
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year of Qianlong he impeached Yunnan Governor Nuomuqin as incompetent and had him recalled;

sentences.zh: 又奏車裡宣慰土司刀維屏逃匿，請裁土缺設專營，上從其議，定營名曰普安。

translations.literal: he also memorialized that Cheli Pacification Commissioner Tusi Daoweiping had fled and hidden and requested that the native post be abolished and a dedicated garrison established; the Emperor approved his proposal and fixed the garrison name as Pu'an.
translations.idiomatic: he also abolished Cheli's fleeing tusi Daoweiping's post for a dedicated Pu'an garrison.

sentences.zh: 尋實授雲貴總督。

translations.literal: Soon he was substantively appointed Governor-General of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon confirmed as Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，以病請解任。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, he requested relief from office on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year of Qianlong he asked to retire for illness.

sentences.zh: 王錫事發，奪官，逮京師論斬。

translations.literal: When Wang Xi's case came to light, he was stripped of office, arrested, and sent to the capital for sentencing to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi's case brought his arrest, dismissal, and capital sentence.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，卒於獄。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, he died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: He died in prison in year 42.

sentences.zh: 徐嗣曾，字宛東，實楊氏，出為徐氏後，浙江海寧人。

translations.literal: Xu Siceng, styled Wandong, was actually of the Yang clan but had been adopted into the Xu clan; he was a native of Haining, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Siceng (Wandong), born Yang but adopted Xu, came from Haining, Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十八年進士，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Qianlong he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed a Principal in the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: A Qianlong 28 jinshi, he entered the Board of Revenue as a principal.

sentences.zh: 再遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director.

sentences.zh: 四十年，授雲南迤東道。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year, he was appointed Intendant of Yidong Circuit, Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year of Qianlong he became Yunnan Yidong intendant.

sentences.zh: 累遷福建布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Financial Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Fujian Financial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五十年，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year of Qianlong he became governor.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，台灣民林爽文為亂，調浙江兵，經延平吉溪塘，兵有溺者，嗣曾坐不能督察，下吏議。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year, the Taiwan commoner Lin Shuangwen raised rebellion; Zhejiang troops were mobilized; passing Jixi Pond in Yanping, some soldiers drowned; Siceng was held accountable for failure to supervise and inspect; the case went to the legal offices for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year of Qianlong Lin Shuangwen rebelled in Taiwan; Zhejiang troops drowned at Yanping's Jixi Pond, and Siceng was faulted for poor oversight.

sentences.zh: 亂既定，五十三年，命赴台灣勘建城垣，因命偕福康安、李侍堯按柴大紀貪劣狀，上責嗣曾平日緘默不言。

translations.literal: After the rebellion was settled, in the fifty-third year he was ordered to proceed to Taiwan to survey and build city walls; he was therefore also ordered to join Fuk'anggan and Li Shiyao in investigating Chai Daji's corruption and misconduct; the Emperor rebuked Siceng for remaining silent in daily affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year of Qianlong he was sent to rebuild Taiwan's walls and, with Fuk'anggan and Li Shiyao, to probe Chai Daji—the Emperor scolded his usual silence.

sentences.zh: 尋疏言大紀廢弛行伍，貪婪營私，事蹟昭著。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized that Daji had neglected the ranks, was greedy and pursued private gain, and that the facts were clear.
translations.idiomatic: He then detailed Chai Daji's slack discipline and graft.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「撫卹被難流民，給銀折米，福建舊例，石準銀二兩；

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Relief for refugees from the disaster, giving silver converted to rice, was an old Fujian precedent of two taels of silver per shi;
translations.idiomatic: He proposed raising disaster relief from Fujian's old rate of two taels per shi of rice

sentences.zh: 今以米貴，請改為三兩。」

translations.literal: now because rice is dear, it is requested that this be changed to three taels.
translations.idiomatic: to three taels because rice had grown costly.

sentences.zh: 上以福康安奏晴雨及時，歲可豐收，仍令視舊例。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Fuk'anggan had memorialized that rain and sun were timely and the year could be bountiful, still ordered that the old precedent be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan reported a good harvest coming, so the Emperor kept the old rate.

sentences.zh: 偕福康安等奏清察積弊，籌酌善後諸事，均得旨允行。

translations.literal: Together with Fuk'anggan and others he memorialized on clearing accumulated abuses and deliberating measures for sound aftermath; all received imperial approval for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: With Fuk'anggan he cleared abuses and planned recovery measures—all approved.

sentences.zh: 嘗以台灣吏治廢弛，不能早行覺察，自劾，上原之。

translations.literal: He once memorialized impeaching himself because Taiwan's official governance was lax and he had not detected problems early; the Emperor pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He self-impeached for failing to spot Taiwan's lax governance early; the Emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 命台灣建福康安、海蘭察生祠，以嗣曾並列。

translations.literal: An order was issued to build living shrines to Fuk'anggan and Hailancha in Taiwan, with Siceng listed alongside them.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan was ordered to build living shrines to Fuk'anggan and Hailancha with Siceng beside them.

sentences.zh: 尋奏台灣海疆刁悍，治亂用嚴，民為盜及殺人者，役殃民，兵冒糧，及助戰守義民或挾嫌害良，皆立置典刑，以是稱上旨，嘉嗣曾不負任使。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized that Taiwan's coastal frontier was fierce and obstinate, that disorder required severity, that commoners who became bandits or killed people, corvée laborers who harmed the people, soldiers who falsely claimed rations, and righteous militia who aided defense but bore grudges and harmed the innocent—all should be immediately subjected to statutory punishment; for this he was said to accord with the imperial intent, and the Emperor praised Siceng for not failing his commission.
translations.idiomatic: He urged harsh justice for Taiwan's bandits, corrupt soldiers, and false militia—the Emperor praised him for meeting the moment.

sentences.zh: 事觕定，命內渡，尋又命俟總兵奎林至乃行。

translations.literal: When the rough work was settled, he was ordered to cross back to the mainland; soon he was again ordered to wait until Regional Commander Kui Lin arrived before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered inland when the crisis eased, he was told to wait for Regional Commander Kui Lin.

sentences.zh: 莊大田者，與爽文同亂，坐誅，嗣曾捕得其子天畏及用事者黃天養送京師，又得海盜，立誅之。

translations.literal: Zhuang Datian, who had rebelled with Shuangwen, was executed; Siceng captured his son Tianwei and the operative Huang Tianyang and sent them to the capital; he also captured pirates and immediately executed them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhuang Datian's son Tianwei and agent Huang Tianyang to the capital, executed pirates on the spot.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，賜孔雀翎、大小荷包。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year, he was granted a peacock feather and large and small purses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year of Qianlong he received a peacock feather and imperial purses.

sentences.zh: 圖像紫光閣。

translations.literal: His portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Glaze.
translations.idiomatic: His portrait entered the Hall of Purple Glaze.

sentences.zh: 請入覲，未行，安南阮光平據黎城，福康安督兵赴廣西，嗣曾署總督。

translations.literal: He requested to enter audience but had not yet departed when Nguyen Quang Binh of Annam seized the Le capital; Fuk'anggan led troops to Guangxi, and Siceng served as acting Governor-General.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could go to court, Nguyen Quang Binh seized Annam; Fuk'anggan marched to Guangxi and Siceng acted as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 福康安瀕行，奏福建文武廢弛，宜大加懲創，上諭嗣曾振刷整頓。

translations.literal: Before departing, Fuk'anggan memorialized that Fujian's civil and military officials were lax and should be severely punished; the Emperor instructed Siceng to shake up and rectify matters.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan warned that Fujian's officials were slack; the Emperor told Siceng to crack down.

sentences.zh: 嗣曾奏許琉球市大黃，限三五百斤，諭不可因噎廢食。

translations.literal: Siceng memorialized permitting Ryukyu to trade in rhubarb, limited to three to five hundred jin; an edict said one must not reject something entirely because of one mishap.
translations.idiomatic: He allowed Ryukyu limited rhubarb trade; the Emperor warned against overreacting.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「福建民多聚族而居，有為盜，責族正舉首，教約有方，給頂帶；

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Many Fujian people live gathered by clan; when there are bandits, the clan elder should be charged to report them; if instruction and restraint are effective, a rank insignia should be granted;
translations.idiomatic: He proposed making clan elders report bandits among Fujian's tight-knit communities, rewarding those who kept order,

sentences.zh: 盜但附從行劫未殺人拒捕，自首，擬斬監候，三年發遣，免死。」

translations.literal: bandits who merely followed in robbery without killing or resisting arrest, if they surrender themselves, should be sentenced to decapitation with delay of execution, exile after three years, and exemption from death.
translations.idiomatic: and letting accomplices who did not kill surrender for delayed execution and exile instead of death.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「捕盜責在將吏。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Capturing bandits is the responsibility of generals and officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied that catching bandits was officers' job,

sentences.zh: 令族正舉首，設將吏何用？

translations.literal: If clan elders are charged to report them, what use are generals and officials?
translations.idiomatic: not clan elders'—

sentences.zh: 族正皆土豪，假以事權，將何所不為？

translations.literal: Clan elders are all local bullies; if false authority is lent them, what will they not do?
translations.idiomatic: and that empowering local bullies as clan elders would invite abuse.

sentences.zh: 福建多盜，當嚴治。

translations.literal: Fujian has many bandits and should be strictly governed.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian needed stern policing, not soft surrender rules.

sentences.zh: 若行劫後尚許自首免死，何以示儆？

translations.literal: If after robbery surrender is still permitted to escape death, how can warning be shown?
translations.idiomatic: Letting robbers off by surrender would destroy deterrence.

sentences.zh: 二條俱屬錯謬。」

translations.literal: Both provisions are entirely mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were rejected outright.

translations.literal: (End of edict.)
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the imperial reply.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，高宗八旬萬壽，台灣生番頭人請赴京祝嘏，嗣曾以聞，命率詣熱河行在瞻覲。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, for the Gaozong Emperor's eightieth birthday, Taiwan aboriginal chiefs requested to go to the capital to offer congratulations; Siceng reported this; he was ordered to lead them to the imperial residence at Rehe for audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year of Qianlong, for the Emperor's eightieth birthday, Taiwan aboriginal chiefs asked to congratulate at Rehe and Siceng was told to escort them.

sentences.zh: 十一月，回任，次山東台莊，病作，遂卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, returning to his post, he stopped at Taizhuang, Shandong; illness struck, and he died there.
translations.idiomatic: Returning in month 11 he fell ill at Shandong's Taizhuang and died.

sentences.zh: 陳步瀛，字麟洲，江南江寧人。

translations.literal: Chen Buying, styled Linzhou, was a native of Jiangning, Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Buying (Linzhou) came from Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十六年會試第一，選庶吉士，改兵部主事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Qianlong he placed first in the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was transferred to Principal in the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: Top of the Qianlong 26 palace exam, he became a Hanlin bachelor then a Board of War principal.

sentences.zh: 累擢郎中，外授河南陳州知府。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Director and was sent out as Prefect of Chenzhou, Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director, then left the capital as Chenzhou prefect in Henan.

sentences.zh: 再遷山西按察使。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He became Shanxi Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋以山西獄訟繁多，改命長麟，仍留步瀛蘭州道。

translations.literal: Soon, because litigation in Shanxi was numerous, Chang Lin was appointed instead, while Buying was retained as Intendant of Lanzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Litigation overwhelmed Shanxi, so Chang Lin took that post while Buying stayed as Lanzhou intendant.

sentences.zh: 旋授甘肅按察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Gansu Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 薩拉爾回蘇四十三亂既定，四十九年，鹽茶廳回田五复據石峰堡為亂，總督李侍堯率兵討之，以步瀛從，捕治諸亂回家屬。

translations.literal: After the Salar Muslim Su Forty-three's rebellion was settled, in the forty-ninth year the Yancha Subprefecture Muslim Tian Wu again seized Shifeng Fort and rebelled; Governor-General Li Shiyao led troops to suppress him, and Buying accompanied him, capturing and punishing the families of the rebel households.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Forty-three's Salar revolt, Tian Wu seized Shifeng Fort in year 49; Buying joined Li Shiyao's campaign and rounded up rebels' families.

sentences.zh: 旋奏令赴安定、會寧督餉，行次隆德，聞副都統明善戰死高廟山，步瀛以靜寧、隆德、平涼諸州縣當下隴要衝，靜寧駐兵三百，請益兵。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized ordering him to proceed to Anding and Huining to supervise provisions; en route at Longde, he heard that Vice Commander Mingshan had died in battle at Gaomiao Mountain; Buying, because Jingning, Longde, Pingliang, and other prefectures and counties lay on the critical lower Long corridor, with three hundred troops stationed at Jingning, requested additional troops.
translations.idiomatic: Heading to Anding and Huining for supplies, he learned Mingshan had fallen at Gaomiao; he asked for more troops to hold the Long corridor.

sentences.zh: 步瀛調固原兵五百赴平涼、隆德守，為犄角；

translations.literal: Buying transferred five hundred troops from Guyuan to Pingliang and Longde for defense, forming pincers;
translations.idiomatic: He shifted five hundred Guyuan troops to Pingliang and Longde as pincers;

sentences.zh: 復往靜寧收明善餘兵守隘，上獎許之，尋諭：「步瀛兵事徑行陳奏，不必拘體制。」

translations.literal: he again went to Jingning to gather Mingshan's remaining troops to guard the passes; the Emperor commended this; soon an edict said: "Buying may memorialize directly on military affairs without being bound by bureaucratic form.
translations.idiomatic: then rallied Mingshan's survivors at Jingning—the Emperor praised him and let him report military matters directly.

sentences.zh: 步瀛奏：「臣收明善餘兵，尚存九百有奇。

translations.literal: Buying memorialized: "Your subject gathered Mingshan's remaining troops; more than nine hundred still remain.
translations.idiomatic: Buying reported over nine hundred of Mingshan's troops still fit for duty.

sentences.zh: 石峰堡回越隆德犯靜寧，平涼知府王立柱督兵民擊之，回退據翠屏山。

translations.literal: Shifeng Fort Muslims crossed Longde and attacked Jingning; Pingliang Prefect Wang Lizhu led soldiers and civilians to repel them; the Muslims retreated and held Cuiping Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Wu's men struck Jingning via Longde; Prefect Wang Lizhu drove them to Cuiping Mountain.

sentences.zh: 靜寧距省五百餘裡、中間會寧、安定為糧運要道。

translations.literal: Jingning is more than five hundred li from the provincial capital; Huining and Anding between them are critical routes for grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Jingning lay 500 li from the capital with Huining and Anding on the grain route.

sentences.zh: 慮回自靜寧南竄襲我師之後，已禀督臣發重兵防護。」

translations.literal: Fearing the Muslims might slip south from Jingning and strike our army's rear, he had already reported to the governor-general requesting heavy troops for protection.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a southern flank attack, he had already asked the governor-general for heavy reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 旋疏報靜寧圍解，並籌濟南、西二路官軍糧餉藥彈，稱上旨。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized reporting that the siege of Jingning was lifted and also planned grain, pay, and ammunition for the official armies on the southern and western routes; this accorded with the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: He then reported Jingning relieved and organized supplies for both southern and western columns.

sentences.zh: 上命大學士阿桂視師，以福康安代侍堯為總督。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Grand Secretary Agui to inspect the army and Fuk'anggan to replace Shiyao as governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Agui to command the front and Fuk'anggan to replace Li Shiyao.

sentences.zh: 上諭以軍事諮步瀛，擢布政使。

translations.literal: An edict said military affairs should be consulted with Buying, and he was promoted to Financial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor put him in charge of military counsel and made him Financial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 福康安奏：「步瀛明白誠實，督餉甚力，但才具不如浦霖。」

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan memorialized: "Buying is clear and honest and supervises provisions with great effort, but his capacity is not equal to Pu Lin's.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan praised Buying's honest supply work but rated him below Pu Lin.

sentences.zh: 命調安徽布政使。

translations.literal: He was ordered transferred to Financial Commissioner of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Anhui Financial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 事定論功，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled and merit was assessed, he was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he received a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 江、淮大饑，民脅眾劫奪。

translations.literal: Great famine struck the Yangtze and Huai regions, and the people coerced one another in mass robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Famine on the Yangtze and Huai drove crowds into banditry.

sentences.zh: 步瀛行縣，督吏賑恤，而捕治其不法者，自夏迄秋，事漸定。

translations.literal: Buying toured the counties, supervising officials in relief, while capturing and punishing the lawless; from summer until autumn the situation gradually stabilized.
translations.idiomatic: He toured counties, relieving famine and punishing looters until order returned by autumn.

sentences.zh: 步瀛以勞瘁致疾，五十四年，擢貴州巡撫，疾大作，卒。

translations.literal: Buying fell ill from exhaustion; in the fifty-fourth year he was promoted to Governor of Guizhou; his illness grew severe, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Worn out by the effort, he was made Guizhou Governor in year 54 but died of the strain.

sentences.zh: 孫永清，字宏度，江南金匱人。

translations.literal: Sun Yongqing, styled Hongdu, was a native of Jin Gui, Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yongqing (Hongdu) came from Jin Gui, Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十三年舉人，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year of Qianlong he passed the provincial examination and was appointed a Secretariat Drafter in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: A Qianlong 33 provincial graduate, he entered the Grand Secretariat as a drafter.

sentences.zh: 永清未入官，嘗佐廣東布政使胡文伯幕。

translations.literal: Before Yongqing entered office, he had once assisted on the staff of Guangdong Financial Commissioner Hu Wenbo.
translations.idiomatic: Before official service he had served on Guangdong Financial Commissioner Hu Wenbo's staff.

sentences.zh: 土司以爭襲相訐，驗文牒皆明印，大吏欲以私造符信罪之。

translations.literal: Native chiefs sued one another over disputed succession; when the documents were verified they all bore official seals; the high officials wished to charge them with privately forging credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Tusi feuding over succession produced sealed documents; superiors wanted to charge them with forgery.

sentences.zh: 永清具稿請文伯力陳，得免者二百餘人。

translations.literal: Yongqing drafted a memorial asking Wenbo to argue forcefully; more than two hundred people were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqing's draft persuaded Wenbo to intervene, sparing over two hundred men.

sentences.zh: 旋充軍機處章京，撰擬精當，事至輒倚以辦。

translations.literal: Soon he served as a clerk in the Grand Council; his drafts were precise and apt, and whenever business arrived they relied on him to handle it.
translations.idiomatic: As a Grand Council clerk his drafts were so reliable that urgent business always went to him.

sentences.zh: 遷侍讀。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Reader.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，雲南總督圖思德奏緬甸將遣使入貢，上遣大學士阿桂往蒞，以永清從。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, Yunnan Governor-General Tusi De memorialized that Burma would send envoys to offer tribute; the Emperor dispatched Grand Secretary Agui to preside, with Yongqing accompanying him.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year of Qianlong, when Tusi De reported Burmese tribute envoys, Agui went to Yunnan with Yongqing.

sentences.zh: 緬甸使不至，阿桂令永清撰檄諭之，送所留守備蘇爾相還。

translations.literal: The Burmese envoys did not arrive; Agui ordered Yongqing to draft a proclamation rebuking them and to return the detained frontier officer Su Erxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When no envoys came, Agui had Yongqing draft a rebuke and return detained officer Su Erxiang.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，授刑部郎中。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, he was appointed Director in the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year of Qianlong he became a Board of Punishments director.

sentences.zh: 考選江西道監察御史。

translations.literal: He was selected through examination as Investigating Censor of the Jiangxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Examination made him Jiangxi Circuit investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，超授左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, he was exceptionally appointed Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year of Qianlong he was unusually promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 授貴州布政使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Financial Commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became Guizhou Financial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 奏言柞子廠產黑鉛，課餘三十餘萬斤，請以十萬斤運廣。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the Zhazichang produced black lead, with a surplus levy of more than three hundred thousand jin, and requested that one hundred thousand jin be transported to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed shipping 100,000 jin of Zhazichang's 300,000-jin lead surplus to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, he served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year of Qianlong he acted as governor.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「柞子廠黑鉛，例於四川永寧設局收發，課餘三百萬斤，請歲以五十萬運存永寧。」

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Black lead from the Zhazichang, by precedent collected and distributed at an office set up at Yongning, Sichuan, has a surplus levy of three million jin; it is requested that five hundred thousand jin be transported and stored at Yongning each year.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to store 500,000 jin yearly of Zhazichang's three-million-jin lead surplus at Yongning, Sichuan.

translations.literal: (End of memorial.)
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the memorial.

sentences.zh: 五十年，擢廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, he was promoted to Governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year of Qianlong he became Guangxi Governor.

sentences.zh: 劾新寧知州金自等逋稅，按察使杜琮、鹽道周延俊等並坐奪官。

translations.literal: He impeached Xinning Prefect Jin Zi and others for tax arrears; Surveillance Commissioner Du Cong and Salt Controller Zhou Yanjun and others were also stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Xinning Prefect Jin Zi for tax arrears, taking down Surveillance Commissioner Du Cong and Salt Controller Zhou Yanjun.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，台灣民林爽文為亂，徵廣西兵，永清奏：「兵出征，在例馬兵賞、借銀各十兩，步兵賞、借銀各六兩，請於借銀留三兩為製衣。」

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year, when the Taiwan commoner Lin Shuangwen rebelled and Guangxi troops were mobilized, Yongqing memorialized: "When troops go on campaign, by precedent cavalry receive ten taels each in reward and loan silver, and infantry six taels each in reward and loan silver; it is requested that three taels of the loan silver be retained for making clothes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year of Qianlong, mobilizing Guangxi troops for Taiwan, he asked to keep three taels of each soldier's loan silver for uniforms.

sentences.zh: 命議敘。

translations.literal: An order was issued to record merit.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved for merit recording.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，藤縣獄系盜梁美煥謀穴牆逃，捕得，永清令立誅之，奏聞，上諭曰：「獄囚反獄劫獄當立誅，若鑽穴越牆，祗求苟免，不得與此同科。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year, the Teng County prisoner-bandit Liang Meihuan plotted to tunnel through the wall and escape; captured, Yongqing ordered immediate execution and memorialized; an edict said: "Prisoners who rebel in prison or rob a prison should be immediately executed; if they merely bore through a wall to cross over, seeking only to escape, they must not be punished the same.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year of Qianlong he summarily executed tunneling prisoner Liang Meihuan; the Emperor said wall-breakers seeking escape were not the same as jail rebels.

sentences.zh: 今之督撫皆好殺弄權，永清失之太過。」

translations.literal: Today's governors and governors-general all delight in killing and wielding power; Yongqing went too far.
translations.idiomatic: Governors today love killing; Yongqing had overreached.

translations.literal: (End of edict.)
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the imperial reply.

sentences.zh: 安南阮惠為亂，國王黎維祁出亡，其臣阮輝宿護維祁母、妻、宗族至龍州，永清及總督孫士毅疏聞。

translations.literal: Nguyen Hui of Annam raised rebellion; King Le Duy Ky fled; his minister Ruan Hui Su escorted Ky's mother, wife, and clan to Longzhou; Yongqing and Governor-General Sun Shiyi memorialized reporting this.
translations.idiomatic: When Nguyen Hui rebelled in Annam, King Le Duy Ky fled; minister Ruan Hui Su brought the royal family to Longzhou, and Yongqing reported it.

sentences.zh: 士毅尋發兵討惠，永清出駐南寧，奏太平設軍需局，以福建延建邵道陸有仁、桂林知府查淳董其事。

translations.literal: Shiyi soon sent troops to suppress Hui; Yongqing proceeded to Nanning and memorialized establishing a military supply bureau at Taiping, with Fujian Yanjian-Shao Circuit Intendant Lu Youren and Guilin Prefect Cha Chun directing the affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shiyi marched against Hui while Yongqing set up a Taiping supply bureau under Lu Youren and Cha Chun.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，維祁復國，使迎其母、妻、宗族，永清為具行李，並傳上旨賚錦緞、綢、布及白金四百。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year, when Duy Ky restored his state, envoys came to welcome his mother, wife, and clan; Yongqing prepared their baggage and also conveyed the imperial bestowal of brocade, silk, cloth, and four hundred taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year of Qianlong, when Le Duy Ky restored his throne, Yongqing equipped the returning royal family and delivered imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 諭獎永清自駐南寧，彈壓邊關，籌辦餉糈，措置得宜，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: An edict praised Yongqing for personally stationing at Nanning, suppressing the frontier passes, organizing provisions, and arranging matters properly; he was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Praised for holding Nanning and managing frontier supplies, he received a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 士毅師敗還，福康安代為總督。

translations.literal: When Shiyi's army was defeated and returned, Fuk'anggan replaced him as governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Shiyi's defeat Fuk'anggan became governor-general.

sentences.zh: 永清與福康安奏：「安南用兵，關內外支放銀百萬、米八萬餘，逐款詳覈，例可用而未用，或用不及數者，以實用之數具報。

translations.literal: Yongqing and Fuk'anggan memorialized: "For the Annam campaign, inside and outside the passes more than a million taels of silver and more than eighty thousand shi of rice were disbursed; each item was examined in detail; where precedent allowed but was unused, or where use fell short of the allotted amount, the actual amount used should be reported.
translations.idiomatic: With Fuk'anggan he reported Annam war costs—over a million taels and 80,000 shi—item by item as actually spent.

sentences.zh: 如有軍行緊急，略有變通。

translations.literal: If there was urgent military need, slight adjustments were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Emergency adjustments were allowed when necessary.

sentences.zh: 與例不符者，仍如例覈減。」

translations.literal: Where this did not match precedent, reduction should still be assessed according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Anything beyond precedent would still be cut to standard.

sentences.zh: 上諭令以實為之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that this be done in accordance with facts.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered honest accounting.

sentences.zh: 秋，以廣西秋審冊自緩決改情實凡三案，諭責永清寬縱。

translations.literal: In autumn, because in the Guangxi autumn review register three cases were changed from delayed execution to confirmed guilt, an edict rebuked Yongqing for leniency.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn three Guangxi death sentences he had softened were reversed and he was rebuked for leniency.

sentences.zh: 東蘭州安置台灣降人鄭管、陳廷乘舟走，追捕，以溺水報。

translations.literal: At Donglan Prefecture, the Taiwan surrenderers Zheng Guan and Chen Ting took boats and fled; pursued, they were reported drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan surrenderers Zheng Guan and Chen Ting fled Donglan by boat and were reported drowned in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 上命奪知州黃圖等官逮訊，永清坐降調，命留任。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Prefect Huang Tu and others stripped of office and arrested for interrogation; Yongqing was demoted in rank but ordered to remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Huang Tu was arrested; Yongqing was demoted but kept in post.

sentences.zh: 是時阮惠更名光平，上封為安南國王，請以來年詣京師祝萬壽，使阮宏匡等叩關入貢。

translations.literal: At this time Nguyen Hui changed his name to Quang Binh; the Emperor enfeoffed him as King of Annam; he requested to go to the capital the following year to congratulate on the imperial birthday; he sent Ruan Hongkuang and others to knock at the border gate and offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Nguyen Hui, now Quang Binh and enfeoffed king of Annam, asked to celebrate the Emperor's birthday in Beijing and sent Ruan Hongkuang with tribute.

sentences.zh: 永清令在太平候旨，疏聞。

translations.literal: Yongqing ordered them to wait at Taiping and memorialized reporting this.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqing held the envoys at Taiping and reported.

sentences.zh: 上令光平使臣於來年燈節前至京師，與外籓蒙古等一體入宴，責永清拘泥。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Quang Binh's envoys to reach the capital before the Lantern Festival of the coming year and enter the banquet together with outer vassals such as Mongolia; Yongqing was rebuked for being rigid.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wanted them in Beijing by Lantern Festival with other vassals and scolded Yongqing's rigidity.

sentences.zh: 永清旋奏光平使臣自桂林北行。

translations.literal: Yongqing soon memorialized that Quang Binh's envoys were traveling north from Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqing then reported the envoys heading north from Guilin.

sentences.zh: 上察廣西學政潘曾起不稱職，以諮永清，永清言曾起性情褊急，未愜士心。

translations.literal: The Emperor, finding Guangxi Education Commissioner Pan Cengqi unfit for office, consulted Yongqing; Yongqing said Cengqi's temperament was narrow and impatient and did not satisfy scholars' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about Education Commissioner Pan Cengqi, Yongqing said the man's temper alienated scholars.

sentences.zh: 上責永清不先奏劾，以方料理安南內附，光平將入覲，不遽易人，罰養廉二年。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked Yongqing for not memorializing impeachment earlier; because Annam's submission was then being handled and Quang Binh would soon enter audience, personnel was not hastily changed; two years' integrity-pay was fined.
translations.idiomatic: Rebuked for not impeaching Pan earlier, he was fined two years' integrity-pay while Annam business continued.

sentences.zh: 五十五年春，光平又以新賜印並御製詩使叩關入貢，永清疏以應否令光平使詣京師請旨。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifty-fifth year, Quang Binh again sent envoys with the newly granted seal and imperial poems to knock at the border gate and offer tribute; Yongqing memorialized asking whether Quang Binh's envoys should be ordered to proceed to the capital, requesting instructions.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 55 Quang Binh sent envoys with a new seal and imperial poems; Yongqing asked whether they should proceed to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「光平遣使陳貢，自應令詣京師，何必奏請？」

translations.literal: An edict said: "When Quang Binh sends envoys presenting tribute, they should naturally be ordered to proceed to the capital—why memorialize and request instructions?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said tribute envoys should simply go to Beijing—no need to ask.

sentences.zh: 永清又奏太平、南寧、鎮安三府與安南接壤，請屯兵防隘，立柵開壕，分隸龍憑、馗纛二營管轄，報聞。

translations.literal: Yongqing also memorialized that Taiping, Nanning, and Zhen'an three prefectures bordered Annam and requested garrison troops at strategic passes, building palisades and digging moats, divided under the jurisdiction of the Longping and Kuizao two garrisons; this was reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed garrisoning Taiping, Nanning, and Zhen'an along the Annam border under Longping and Kuizao garrisons.

sentences.zh: 四月，光平入關，以其子光垂、臣吳文楚從，奏聞，上嘉之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Quang Binh entered the pass, with his son Quang Chui and minister Wu Wenchu accompanying; this was memorialized; the Emperor commended this.
translations.idiomatic: In month 4 Quang Binh entered the border with his son Quang Chui and minister Wu Wenchu—the Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 弟籓，監生。

translations.literal: His younger brother Fan was a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Fan was an Imperial Academy student.

sentences.zh: 以四庫館議敘，授中書科中書。

translations.literal: Through merit assessment in the Siku Quanshu project, he was appointed a Drafter in the Secretariat Chancery.
translations.idiomatic: Siku Quanshu service made him a Secretariat Chancery drafter.

sentences.zh: 官至安徽布政使。

translations.literal: He rose to Financial Commissioner of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Anhui Financial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 子爾準，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Erzhun has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Erzhun has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 郭世勳，漢軍正紅旗人。

translations.literal: Guo Shixun was a Han Chinese bannerman of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shixun, a Plain Red Han bannerman.

sentences.zh: 初自筆帖式擢吏部主事。

translations.literal: At first, from clerk he was promoted to Principal in the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: From clerk he rose to a Board of Civil Appointments principal.

sentences.zh: 選福建龍巖知州。

translations.literal: He was selected as Prefect of Longyan, Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He became Longyan prefect in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 五遷湖南布政使。

translations.literal: After five promotions he became Financial Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Five promotions made him Hunan Financial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十四年，擢貴州巡撫，調廣東。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year of Qianlong, he was promoted to Governor of Guizhou and transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 54 he became Guizhou Governor, then moved to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「廣東有洋商鹽務，為腥羶之地。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Guangdong has foreign merchants and salt affairs—it is a place of fishy stench.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor warned that Guangdong's foreign trade and salt were a tainted arena,

sentences.zh: 世勳操守廉潔，治事勤實，務慎持素履。」

translations.literal: Shixun's integrity is clean and his handling of affairs diligent and solid; he must carefully maintain his plain conduct.
translations.idiomatic: but praised Shixun's clean, diligent record and urged him to keep it.

sentences.zh: 監臨鄉試，奏額送科舉多取數百名，經費由督撫捐貲備辦，諭國家無此政體，不允。

translations.literal: Supervising the provincial examination, he memorialized sending many hundreds more examination candidates than the quota, with expenses prepared by the governor-general and governor from donated funds; an edict said the state has no such policy and did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed overshooting exam quotas at governors' expense; the throne rejected it as unorthodox.

sentences.zh: 奏禁大黃出洋，西洋各國歲不過五百斤，瓊州、台灣亦如之；

translations.literal: He memorialized prohibiting rhubarb export overseas; Western countries each year no more than five hundred jin, and Qiongzhou and Taiwan likewise;
translations.idiomatic: He capped rhubarb exports at 500 jin for Western nations, Qiongzhou, and Taiwan;

sentences.zh: 暹羅、安南貢船至，亦五百斤。

translations.literal: when Siam and Annam tribute ships arrived, likewise five hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: Siam and Annam tribute ships got the same limit.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，總督福康安入覲，命世勳署兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, when Governor-General Fuk'anggan entered audience, Shixun was ordered to serve as acting Governor-General of Guangdong and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year of Qianlong, while Fuk'anggan went to court, Shixun acted as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 劾雷瓊鎮總兵葉至剛誤民為匪，左江鎮總兵普吉保濫刑斃命，皆論罪如律。

translations.literal: He impeached Lei-Qiong Garrison Commander Ye Zhigang for wrongly treating people as bandits, and Zuojiang Garrison Commander Pu Jibao for abusive punishment causing death; all were punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He punished Lei-Qiong commander Ye Zhigang for false bandit arrests and Zuojiang commander Pu Jibao for fatal torture.

sentences.zh: 參將錢邦彥巡洋崖州，遇盜被戕，上以福康安詣京師後，世勳不能整飭，嚴斥之。

translations.literal: Major Pu Bangyan patrolled the coast at Yazhou and encountered bandits and was killed; the Emperor, because after Fuk'anggan went to the capital Shixun could not rectify discipline, severely rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Major Pu Bangyan was killed by pirates off Yazhou; the Emperor scolded Shixun for lax discipline after Fuk'anggan left.

sentences.zh: 暹羅國王鄭華諮：「乾隆三十一年被烏圖構兵圍城，國君被陷。

translations.literal: The King of Siam Zheng Hua petitioned: "In the thirty-first year of Qianlong, Wutu raised troops and besieged the city; the king was trapped.
translations.idiomatic: Siam's King Zheng Hua petitioned that in Qianlong 31 Burma's Wutu besieged his capital and trapped the king.

sentences.zh: 其父昭克復舊基，十僅五六。

translations.literal: His father Zhao recovered the old foundation, only five or six tenths remaining.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhao recovered only half the old realm.

sentences.zh: 舊有丹蓍氏、麻叨、塗坯三城，仍被佔據。

translations.literal: The three cities formerly held by the Danchi clan—Madao and Tubai—were still occupied.
translations.idiomatic: Burma still held the old cities of Danchi, Madao, and Tubai.

sentences.zh: ​​請代奏令烏圖割還三城。」

translations.literal: He requested memorialization on his behalf ordering Wutu to cede back the three cities.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the court to order Wutu to return the three cities.

sentences.zh: 烏圖即緬甸。

translations.literal: Wutu was Burma.
translations.idiomatic: Wutu was Burma.

sentences.zh: 世勳以其非禮妄幹，留其使廣東，奏聞。

translations.literal: Shixun, because the request was improper and presumptuous interference, detained the envoy in Guangdong and memorialized reporting this.
translations.idiomatic: Shixun detained the envoy in Guangdong as an improper request.

sentences.zh: 上命軍機大臣擬檄，略謂：「故緬甸酋懵駁與暹羅詔氏構兵，非今國王孟隕事。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the Grand Council ministers to draft a dispatch, stating in summary: "The former Burmese chief Mengbo quarreled with Siam's Zhao clan—this is not the present King Mengyun's affair.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Council drafted a reply: old Burma-Siam wars were not King Mengyun's business.

sentences.zh: 暹羅又係異姓繼立，不直追問詔氏已失疆土。

translations.literal: Siam is also a different surname succeeding to the throne; it is not proper to pursue the Zhao clan's already lost territory.
translations.idiomatic: Siam's new dynasty could not reclaim the Zhao clan's lost lands.

sentences.zh: 天朝撫馭萬國，緬甸固新封，暹羅亦至華嗣掌國始加封爵，宜釋嫌修好，共沐寵榮，不得以非分乾求，妄行瑣瀆。」

translations.literal: The Celestial Court cherishes and governs all nations; Burma is indeed newly enfeoffed, and Siam also received enfeoffment only when Zhihua succeeded to rule the state; they should release suspicion and restore good relations, sharing in imperial favor and glory—they must not make improper requests or presumptuously engage in petty importunity.
translations.idiomatic: Both newly enfeoffed states should reconcile and enjoy imperial favor—not make impertinent demands.

sentences.zh: 命世勳與福康安聯銜照會，並告來使，但云：「札商福康安，未經代奏。」

translations.literal: He ordered Shixun and Fuk'anggan to issue a joint note, and also inform the envoy, saying only: "A letter was sent consulting Fuk'anggan; it was not memorialized on your behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Shixun and Fuk'anggan were to notify the envoy only that no memorial had been forwarded.

translations.literal: (End of note.)
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the joint notification.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，世勳奏洋船準攜砲，內地商船不准攜砲。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year, Shixun memorialized that foreign ships were permitted to carry cannon, but domestic merchant ships were not permitted to carry cannon.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year of Qianlong he allowed foreign ships cannon but banned them on domestic merchants.

sentences.zh: 上諭之曰：「商船出洋，攜砲禦盜。

translations.literal: An edict replied: "Merchant ships going overseas carry cannon to defend against bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied that merchant ships needed cannon against pirates.

sentences.zh: 不特各國來船未便禁止，即內地商船遇盜不能禦，豈有束手待斃之理？

translations.literal: It is not convenient to forbid even ships coming from all countries, and when domestic merchant ships encounter bandits they cannot defend—how could there be reason to sit bound waiting for death?
translations.idiomatic: Banning cannon would leave Chinese merchants defenseless at sea.

sentences.zh: 祗令海口將吏察驗，不可因噎廢食。」

translations.literal: Only order frontier officers at the ports to inspect and verify; one must not reject something entirely because of one mishap.
translations.idiomatic: Port officials should inspect ships—not ban cannon outright.

sentences.zh: 上以廣東多械鬥，諭世勳稽察化導。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Guangdong had many armed brawls, instructed Shixun to investigate and guide reform.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong's armed feuds led the Emperor to order Shixun to investigate and reform.

sentences.zh: 有步文斌者，以罪配德慶州，傳習邪教，世勳捕得四十餘人送京師。

translations.literal: One Bu Wenbin, sentenced for crime to Deqing Prefecture, propagated heterodox teachings; Shixun captured more than forty people and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Wenbin, exiled to Deqing for spreading heterodox teachings, was caught with forty followers and sent to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 上諭以其渠送京師，餘令世勳繫獄，候刑部擬罪。

translations.literal: An edict said that the ringleaders should be sent to the capital and the rest ordered imprisoned by Shixun, awaiting the Board of Punishments' sentencing proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Ringleaders went to the capital; the rest awaited sentencing in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，安南國王阮光平諮言：「國境嵩陵等七州毗連雲南開化，莫氏舊人黃公瓚父子據守，夤緣內附，籥懇代奏詳察。」

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year, King Nguyen Quang Binh of Annam petitioned: "Within the borders, the seven prefectures including Songling adjoin Yunnan's Kaihua; old Mo-clan subjects Huang Gongzan, father and son, hold them and have attached themselves by connection to the interior, earnestly begging memorialization for detailed investigation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year of Qianlong Quang Binh claimed seven border prefectures held by Huang Gongzan and his son near Yunnan's Kaihua.

sentences.zh: 使至龍州，龍州通判王撫棠以所請非分，發書駁還。

translations.literal: When the envoy reached Longzhou, Longzhou Subprefect Magistrate Wang Futang, because the request was improper, sent a letter rejecting and returning it.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhou magistrate Wang Futang rejected the request as out of line.

sentences.zh: 世勳奏聞，上嘉撫棠，賜大緞獎之。

translations.literal: Shixun memorialized reporting this; the Emperor commended Futang and granted him large brocade as reward.
translations.idiomatic: Shixun reported it; the Emperor rewarded Wang Futang with brocade.

sentences.zh: 光平又以黎維祁弟維祗結土酋農福縉為亂，遣兵剿滅，具表獻捷。

translations.literal: Quang Binh also reported that Le Duy Ky's younger brother Duy Chi had joined with local chief Nong Fujin to raise rebellion; he dispatched troops to suppress and exterminate them and submitted a memorial reporting victory.
translations.idiomatic: Quang Binh also reported crushing Le Duy Ky's brother Duy Chi and chief Nong Fujin.

sentences.zh: 表內並言：「維祗為亂，因維祁從人丁迓衡等為維祁通消息，請按治維祁罪。」

translations.literal: Within the memorial it also said: "Duy Chi rebelled because Ding Heng and others, followers of Duy Ky, conveyed messages for Duy Ky; it is requested that Duy Ky be punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: His victory report also asked to punish Le Duy Ky for messages sent through follower Ding Heng.

sentences.zh: 世勳以光平所言臆度無憑，對揚失體，照會令將表文刪節，繕正奏聞。

translations.literal: Shixun, because Quang Binh's words were speculative without evidence and his response in audience was improper in form, issued a note ordering the memorial text deleted and revised and then memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Shixun, finding the charge speculative, ordered Quang Binh's report edited before forwarding.

sentences.zh: 上已先得巡撫陳用敷奏，令諭光平具確據，並通消息者何人，送京​​師按治，命世勳遵前旨照會光平。

translations.literal: The Emperor had already received Governor Chen Yongfu's memorial first, ordering Quang Binh to provide solid evidence and also who the message-conveyers were, to be sent to the capital for punishment; Shixun was ordered to follow the previous instruction in issuing a note to Quang Binh.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, having Chen Yongfu's earlier order for proof, told Shixun to demand names and evidence from Quang Binh.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，暹羅、安南貢使至，世勳遣吏伴送詣京師。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, when Siam and Annam tribute envoys arrived, Shixun dispatched clerks to escort them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year of Qianlong he sent clerks to escort Siam and Annam envoys to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 上以所派職卑才庸，慮為外籓所輕，降旨申飭。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because the dispatched officials were low in rank and mediocre in talent, feared outer vassals would look down on them and issued a descending edict of rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked him for sending low-ranking escorts who might disgrace the court.

sentences.zh: 潮州總兵託爾歡請觀，例具清字摺，硃批令來見。

translations.literal: Chaozhou Regional Commander Tuo Erhuan requested an audience; by precedent he submitted a Manchu memorial; vermilion endorsement ordered him to come for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozhou commander Tuo Erhuan requested audience with a Manchu memorial, approved in vermilion.

sentences.zh: 世勳奏委署總兵，譯漢文為俚語，上賜荷包愧之。

translations.literal: Shixun memorialized appointing an acting regional commander and translating the Chinese text into vulgar speech; the Emperor granted a purse in embarrassment.
translations.idiomatic: Shixun reported the appointment in crude translation; the Emperor sent a purse in embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 英吉利遣使入貢，請遣人留京居住，上不許，慮英吉利貢使還經廣東復多所陳乞，時已授長麟兩廣總督，命與世勳和衷商榷。

translations.literal: Britain sent envoys to offer tribute and requested that people be left to reside in the capital; the Emperor did not permit this, fearing that when the British tribute envoys returned via Guangdong they would again make many requests; Chang Lin had already been appointed Governor-General of Guangdong and Guangxi, and he was ordered to consult harmoniously with Shixun.
translations.idiomatic: Britain's tribute mission asked to leave residents in Beijing; refused, Shixun was told to cooperate with new Governor-General Chang Lin when they passed Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 尋奏英吉利貢使請在黃埔蓋房居住，已嚴行拒絕，並禁內地奸民指引勾結，上賜荷包獎之。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized that the British tribute envoys requested to build houses at Whampoa to reside; this had been strictly refused, and inland wicked commoners were forbidden to guide and connect with them; the Emperor granted a purse in reward.
translations.idiomatic: He reported rejecting Britain's Whampoa housing request and blocking local collusion—the Emperor rewarded him with a purse.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，入覲，途次病作，至京師卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year, he entered audience; illness struck en route; he reached the capital and died; sacrificial rites and burial honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year of Qianlong he fell ill on the way to court and died in the capital with funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 畢沅，字纕蘅，江南鎮洋人。

translations.literal: Bi Yuan, styled Xiangheng, was a native of Zhenjiang, Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yuan (Xiangheng) came from Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十八年舉人，授內閣中書，充軍機處章京。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Qianlong he passed the provincial examination, was appointed a Secretariat Drafter in the Grand Secretariat, and served as a clerk in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: A Qianlong 18 provincial graduate, he became a Grand Secretariat drafter and Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 二十五年一甲一名進士，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he placed first in the first rank of the metropolitan examination and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Qianlong he topped the palace exam and became a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 再遷庶子。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，授甘肅鞏秦階道。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, he was appointed Intendant of Gong-Qin-Jie Circuit, Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year of Qianlong he became Gansu Gong-Qin-Jie intendant.

sentences.zh: 從總督明山出關勘屯田，調安肅道。

translations.literal: He accompanied Governor-General Mingshan beyond the pass to survey military colonies and was transferred to Intendant of Ansu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: With Governor-General Mingshan he surveyed frontier colonies, then became Ansu intendant.

sentences.zh: 擢陝西按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He became Shaanxi Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上東巡，覲行在，備言甘肅旱。

translations.literal: When the Emperor toured the east, Yuan attended at the traveling palace and fully reported Gansu's drought.
translations.idiomatic: During the eastern tour he reported Gansu's drought to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 諭治賑，並免逋賦四百萬。

translations.literal: An edict ordered relief administration and also remitted four million in tax arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Relief was ordered and four million in back taxes forgiven.

sentences.zh: 擢布政使，屢護巡撫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Financial Commissioner and repeatedly served as acting governor.
