translations.idiomatic: He became Financial Commissioner and often acted as governor.

sentences.zh: 師徵金川，遣沅督餉，軍無匱，授巡撫。

translations.literal: When the army campaigned in Jinchuan, Yuan was dispatched to supervise provisions; the army suffered no shortage, and he was appointed governor.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to feed the Jinchuan army without shortfall, he was made governor.

sentences.zh: 河、洛、渭並漲，朝邑被水。

translations.literal: The Yellow, Luo, and Wei rivers all rose together, and Chaoyi was inundated.
translations.idiomatic: Floods on the Yellow, Luo, and Wei rivers inundated Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 治賑，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: He administered relief and fully saved very many.
translations.idiomatic: His relief work saved countless lives.

sentences.zh: 幕民墾興平、盩厔、扶風、武功荒地，得田八十餘頃。

translations.literal: He encouraged the people to reclaim wasteland in Xingping, Zhouzhi, Fufeng, and Wugong and obtained more than eighty qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: He opened over eighty qing of wasteland in Xingping, Zhouzhi, Fufeng, and Wugong.

sentences.zh: 濬涇陽龍洞渠，溉民田。

translations.literal: He dredged the Longdong Canal in Jingyang and irrigated the people's fields.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged Jingyang's Longdong Canal to irrigate farmland.

sentences.zh: 嘉峪關外鎮西、迪化士子赴鄉會試者，奏請給驛馬。

translations.literal: For scholars beyond Jiayuguan at Zhenxi and Dihua who went to the provincial and metropolitan examinations, he memorialized requesting relay horses be granted.
translations.idiomatic: He secured relay horses for frontier scholars beyond Jiayuguan traveling to exams.

sentences.zh: 置姬氏五經博士，奉祀文、武、成、康四王及周公陵墓。

translations.literal: He established the Ji clan Five Classics Erudite and offered sacrifices at the tombs of Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang and Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the Ji clan Five Classics Erudite and sacrifices at the Zhou royal tombs.

sentences.zh: 修華嶽廟暨漢、唐以來名跡，收碑碣儲學宮。

translations.literal: He repaired Mount Hua's temple and famous sites from Han and Tang times onward and collected stele inscriptions stored at the school.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Mount Hua's temple and Han-Tang monuments, collecting steles for the school.

sentences.zh: 屢署總督。

translations.literal: He repeatedly served as acting governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: He often acted as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, he was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of Qianlong he received a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，丁母憂，去官。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, he left office upon mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year of Qianlong he left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，陝西巡撫缺員，諭：「沅在西安久，守制將一年。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, when the Shaanxi governorship fell vacant, an edict said: "Yuan has long been in Xi'an; mourning will soon reach one year.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year of Qianlong, with Shaanxi vacant, the Emperor noted Yuan had been in Xi'an nearly a year into mourning

sentences.zh: 命往署理，非開在任守制例也。」

translations.literal: He is ordered to proceed to serve as acting governor—this is not opening the precedent of mourning while in active office.
translations.idiomatic: and ordered him to act as governor—not the usual mourning-in-office rule.

translations.literal: (End of edict.)
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the imperial instruction.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，甘肅撒拉爾回蘇四十三為亂，沅會西安軍伍彌泰、提督馬彪發兵討之。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, the Gansu Salar Muslim Su Forty-three rebelled; Yuan joined Xi'an garrison commander Mi Tai and Regional Commander Ma Biao in dispatching troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year of Qianlong he joined Mi Tai and Ma Biao against Salar rebel Su Forty-three.

sentences.zh: 事平論功，賜一品頂帶。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled and merit was assessed, he was granted first-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: After pacification he received first-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 甘肅冒賑事發，御史錢灃劾沅瞻徇，降三品項戴。

translations.literal: When Gansu's false relief reporting came to light, Censor Qian Feng impeached Yuan for favoritism; he was demoted to third-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Qian Feng caught false relief reports and demoted Yuan to third rank.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，復還原品，尋實授巡撫。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year, his original rank was restored; soon he was substantively appointed governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year of Qianlong his rank was restored and he was confirmed as governor.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，甘肅鹽茶廳回田五复亂，沅遣兵分道搜剿。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, the Yancha Subprefecture Muslim Tian Wu rebelled again; Yuan dispatched troops to search and suppress on separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year of Qianlong Tian Wu rebelled again at Yancha; Yuan sent columns to hunt him down.

sentences.zh: 上命大學士阿桂視師，沅治軍需及驛傳供億，屢得旨獎勵。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Grand Secretary Agui to inspect the army; Yuan managed military supplies and relay provision; he repeatedly received edicts of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: While Agui commanded the front, Yuan ran supplies and won repeated praise.

sentences.zh: 沅先後撫陝西十年，嘗奏：「足民之要，農田為上。

translations.literal: During more than ten years governing Shaanxi in succession, Yuan once memorialized: "The essential for enriching the people is farmland above all.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years in Shaanxi he wrote that enriching the people meant farmland first.

sentences.zh: 關右大川，如涇、渭、灞、滻、灃、滈、潦、潏、河、洛、漆、沮、汧、汭諸水，流長源遠。

translations.literal: The great rivers of the western passes, such as the Jing, Wei, Ba, Chan, Feng, Hao, Liao, Yu, He, Luo, Qi, Ju, Qian, and Rui waters, flow long with distant sources.
translations.idiomatic: The great western rivers—Jing, Wei, Ba, Chan, Feng, Hao, and others—had long courses and distant headwaters.

sentences.zh: 若能就近疏引，築堰開渠，以時蓄洩，自無水旱之虞。

translations.literal: If nearby diversion can be made, dikes built and channels opened, with timely storage and release, naturally there will be no worry of flood or drought.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby irrigation with dikes and channels would end flood-drought cycles.

sentences.zh: 古來雲中、北地、五原、上郡諸處畜牧，為天下饒，若酌籌閒款，市牛羊駝馬，為畀民試牧；

translations.literal: In ancient times Yunzhong, Beidi, Wuyuan, Shangjun, and other places practiced animal husbandry and were the richest under heaven; if spare funds are prudently allocated to purchase cattle, sheep, camels, and horses and give them to the people for trial herding;
translations.idiomatic: He proposed using spare funds to lend livestock for trial herding as in ancient Yunzhong and Beidi,

sentences.zh: 俟有孳生，交還官項，餘則畀其人以為資本。

translations.literal: when there is increase, the principal should be returned to the state account and the remainder given to the person as capital.
translations.idiomatic: with offspring returned to the state and surplus kept as capital.

sentences.zh: 耕作與畜牧相兼，實為邊土無窮之利。」

translations.literal: Combining farming and animal husbandry is truly boundless profit for the frontier soil.
translations.idiomatic: Mixed farming and herding, he argued, would endlessly benefit the frontier.

sentences.zh: 議未行。

translations.literal: The proposal was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was never adopted.

sentences.zh: 五十年，調河南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, he was transferred to Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year of Qianlong he became Henan Governor.

sentences.zh: 奏：「河北諸府患旱，各屬倉儲，蠲緩賑恤，所存無多，請留漕糧二十萬備賑。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The prefectures north of the Yellow River suffer drought; granaries in each subordinate district, with remission, relief, and delayed collection, have little remaining; it is requested that two hundred thousand shi of grain transport be retained for relief.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to hold 200,000 shi of grain transport for drought relief north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 既又請緩徵民欠錢糧，並展賑，上溫諭嘉之。

translations.literal: He then also requested delayed collection of the people's tax arrears in money and grain and extension of relief; the Emperor warmly praised this in an edict.
translations.idiomatic: He also sought tax deferrals and extended relief—the Emperor warmly praised him.

sentences.zh: 命詣胎簪山求淮水真源，御製淮源記以賜。

translations.literal: He was ordered to proceed to Taizanshan to seek the true source of the Huai River; an imperial composition, "Record of the Huai Source," was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Taizanshan to find the Huai's source, he received the imperial "Record of the Huai Source."

sentences.zh: 五十一年，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year, he was granted a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year of Qianlong he received a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 授湖廣總督。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor-General of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He became Huguang Governor-General.

sentences.zh: 伊陽盜秦國棟戕官，上責沅捕治未得，命仍回巡撫。

translations.literal: The bandit Qin Guodong of Yiyang killed an official; the Emperor rebuked Yuan for failing to capture and punish him and ordered him to return to governor's duties.
translations.idiomatic: Rebuked for failing to catch Yiyang bandit Qin Guodong, he was sent back to provincial governor's duties.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，复授湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year, he was again appointed Governor-General of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year of Qianlong he again became Huguang Governor-General.

sentences.zh: 江決荊州，發帑百萬治工。

translations.literal: The river broke at Jingzhou; a million taels from the treasury funded the works.
translations.idiomatic: When the river burst at Jingzhou, a million taels funded repairs.

sentences.zh: 沅奏：「江自松滋下至荊州萬城堤，折而東北流，南逼窖金，荊水至無所宣洩。

translations.literal: Yuan memorialized: "From Songzi downstream to Jingzhou's Wancheng embankment, the river turns and flows northeast, pressing south against Yaojin; when Jing water arrives there is nowhere for discharge.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the Yangtze from Songzi to Jingzhou's Wancheng dike turning northeast with nowhere for the Jing to discharge.

sentences.zh: 請築對岸楊林洲土壩、雞嘴石壩，逼溜南趨，刷洲沙無致雍遏。」

translations.literal: It is requested to build an earthen dam on the opposite-bank Yanglin Isle and a stone dam at Jizui, forcing the current southward, scouring the sand of the isle without causing obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed opposite-bank dams at Yanglin Isle and Jizui to turn the current south and scour sandbars.

sentences.zh: 又請修襄陽老龍堤、常德石櫃堤、潛江仙人堤，鑿四川、湖北大江險灘，便雲南銅運。

translations.literal: He also requested repair of Xiangyang's Laolong Embankment, Changde's Shigui Embankment, and Qianjiang's Xianren Embankment, and dredging dangerous shoals on the great rivers of Sichuan and Hubei to facilitate Yunnan copper transport.
translations.idiomatic: He also sought repairs at Xiangyang, Changde, and Qianjiang and dredging for Yunnan copper transport.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，陝西安康、四川大寧邪教並起，稱傳自湖北，沅赴襄陽、鄖陽按治，降授山東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year, heterodox teachings arose together in Ankang, Shaanxi, and Daning, Sichuan, said to have spread from Hubei; Yuan proceeded to Xiangyang and Yunyang to investigate and punish; he was demoted and appointed Governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year of Qianlong sectarian trouble spread from Hubei; Yuan investigated in Xiangyang and was demoted to Shandong Governor.

sentences.zh: 上以明年歸政，令督撫察民欠錢糧豁免，奏蠲山東積逋四百八十七萬、常平社倉米穀五十萬四千餘石。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because the following year he would return power, ordered governors and governors-general to examine the people's tax arrears in money and grain for remission; Yuan memorialized remitting Shandong's accumulated arrears of four million eight hundred seventy thousand in money and five hundred four thousand-plus shi of ever-normal and community granary grain.
translations.idiomatic: Before abdication the Emperor ordered tax forgiveness; Yuan remitted Shandong's 4.87 million taels and 504,000 shi of granary grain.

sentences.zh: 六十年，仍授湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year, he was again appointed Governor-General of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year of Qianlong he again became Huguang Governor-General.

sentences.zh: 湖南苗石三保等為亂，命赴荊州、常德督餉，以運輸週妥，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: When the Miao Shi Sanbao and others rebelled in Hunan, he was ordered to proceed to Jingzhou and Changde to supervise provisions; because transport was thoroughly handled, he was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: During Hunan Miao rebellions he fed the armies from Jingzhou and Changde and earned a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，枝江民聶人傑等挾邪教為亂，破保康、夾鳳、竹山，圍襄陽，沅自辰州至枝江捕治。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, the Zhijiang commoners Nie Renjie and others, relying on heterodox teachings, rebelled, breaking Baokang, Jiafeng, and Zhushan, besieging Xiangyang; Yuan proceeded from Chenzhou to Zhijiang to capture and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1, Nie Renjie and sectarian rebels took Baokang and besieged Xiangyang; Yuan marched from Chenzhou to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 當陽又陷，复移駐荊州，上命解沅總督。

translations.literal: Dangyang also fell; he again moved his headquarters to Jingzhou; the Emperor ordered Yuan relieved of the governorship-generalship.
translations.idiomatic: When Dangyang fell he moved to Jingzhou and was removed as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 旋克當陽，獲亂渠張正謨等，復命沅為總督如故，予二等輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: Soon Dangyang was recovered and rebel chiefs Zhang Zhengmo and others were captured; Yuan was again appointed governor-general as before and granted the hereditary office of Second-Class Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: After retaking Dangyang and capturing Zhang Zhengmo he was restored with a hereditary Second-Class Commandant of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 尋奏亂渠石三保、吳半生、吳八月等皆就獲，惟石柳鄧未獲；

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized that rebel chiefs Shi Sanbao, Wu Bansheng, Wu Bayue, and others had all been captured, but Shi Liudeng had not yet been captured;
translations.idiomatic: He reported Shi Sanbao, Wu Bansheng, and Wu Bayue captured but Shi Liudeng still at large;

sentences.zh: 請撤各省兵，留二三萬分駐苗疆要隘。

translations.literal: he requested withdrawal of troops from each province, retaining twenty or thirty thousand divided among strategic passes in the Miao frontier.
translations.idiomatic: he asked to withdraw provincial armies, leaving 20–30,000 at Miao frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「撤兵朕所原，但平隴未克，石柳鄧未獲，豈能遽議及此？」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Withdrawal of troops is what We would wish, but Pinglong has not been taken and Shi Liudeng has not been captured—how can this be hastily deliberated?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said withdrawal was fine in principle but premature while Pinglong and Shi Liudeng remained untaken.

sentences.zh: 尋獲石柳鄧。

translations.literal: Soon Shi Liudeng was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Liudeng was soon captured.

sentences.zh: 上命沅馳赴湖南鎮撫。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Yuan to hurry to Hunan to pacify and soothe.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was ordered to Hunan to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「樊城為漢南一都會，請建磚城，以工代賑。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Fancheng is the great gathering place of southern Han; it is requested to build a brick city, using labor in place of relief.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed building Fancheng's brick walls as a work-for-relief project.

sentences.zh: 二年，請以提督移辰州，增設總兵駐花園汛。

translations.literal: In the second year, he requested that the regional commander be moved to Chenzhou and an additional major-general be established stationed at Huayuan Station.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianlong he asked to move the regional commander to Chenzhou and add a major-general at Huayuan.

sentences.zh: 尋報疾作，手足不仁，賜活絡丸。

translations.literal: Soon he reported illness striking, with numbness in hands and feet; the Emperor granted invigorating pills.
translations.idiomatic: He then reported numbness in hands and feet and received imperial pills.

sentences.zh: 旋卒，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: Soon he died; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died and was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 四年，追論沅教匪初起失察貽誤，濫用軍需帑項，奪世職，籍其家。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, a retrospective judgment held that at the first rise of the teaching-bandits Yuan had failed to detect and had delayed, and had wantonly used military supply funds; his hereditary office was stripped and his household property confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qianlong a posthumous reckoning stripped his hereditary rank and confiscated his estate for early sectarian failures and supply abuse.

sentences.zh: 沅以文學起，愛才下士，職事修舉；

translations.literal: Yuan rose through literary accomplishment, loved talent and honored scholars, and performed his duties with diligence;
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yuan rose as a scholar-official who loved talent and ran a tight administration;

sentences.zh: 然不長於治軍，又易為屬吏所蔽，功名遂不終。

translations.literal: yet he was not skilled at governing armies, and was easily misled by subordinate officials, so his fame and achievement did not reach completion.
translations.idiomatic: yet he was no general and let subordinates deceive him, so his career did not end well.

sentences.zh: 論曰：富勒渾、秉恬、鄂寶餫金川之軍，績當臨清之亂，圖思德招緬甸之使，步瀛禦石峰堡之變，嗣曾肅台灣之政，永清受安南之降，世勳屢卻暹羅、安南幹請。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Fu Leihun, Bingtian, and E Bao supplied the Jinchuan army; Ji faced the Linqing rebellion; Tusi De received Burma's envoys; Buying met the Shifeng Fort crisis; Siceng restored Taiwan's governance; Yongqing accepted Annam's surrender; Shixun repeatedly rejected improper requests from Siam and Annam.
translations.idiomatic: The historian notes: these men fed Jinchuan, faced Linqing, handled Burma, Shifeng Fort, Taiwan, Annam, and Siam's importunate petitions.

sentences.zh: 若英吉利入貢，中外交涉，於此萌芽。

translations.literal: When Britain offered tribute, Sino-foreign dealings sprouted here.
translations.idiomatic: Britain's tribute mission marked the beginning of Sino-foreign diplomacy.

sentences.zh: 川、楚教匪，沅當其始，久而後定。

translations.literal: The Sichuan and Hubei teaching-bandits—Yuan faced them at the start; only after long effort was order restored.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yuan faced the Sichuan-Hubei sectarian revolts at their outset; order took years to restore.

sentences.zh: 諸人者皆身膺疆寄，與兵事相表裡，功罪不同，賞罰或異；

translations.literal: These men all personally bore frontier commissions, intertwined with military affairs; merit and fault differ, reward and punishment varied;
translations.idiomatic: All bore frontier responsibility tied to war, with mixed merit, fault, reward, and punishment;

sentences.zh: 欲求其事始末，固不可略焉，故類而錄之。

translations.literal: to seek the beginning and end of their affairs cannot be omitted, and therefore they are grouped and recorded together.
translations.idiomatic: their full stories belong together, which is why they are recorded as a group.
